articles.summary: Betfair te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Real Madrid y al Villarreal en el Santiago Bernabéu, correspondiente a la jornada 8 de LaLiga
articles.body: El Real Madrid recibe al Villarreal este sábado (21:00 h) en el Bernabéu, en el regreso de LaLiga tras el parón de selecciones. El conjunto blanco llega cuarto, con 15 puntos y un balance de cinco victorias y dos derrotas, la última por 2-1 ante el Atlético. El Villarreal es noveno, con 8 puntos tras ganar sus dos últimos partidos de Liga, ambos por 3-1, ante Málaga y Levante. Favorito para el partido entre Real Madrid y Villarreal Las casas de apuestas no dudan. Betfair paga la victoria del Real Madrid a cuota 1.30, por 6 del empate y 7.50 del triunfo visitante. La cuota local equivale a una probabilidad implícita cercana al 77 %. A ello se suma el historial reciente, y es que los blancos han ganado cinco de los últimos seis duelos ligueros ante el Villarreal. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan aparece como una de las opciones más atractivas dentro de las apuestas deportivas, y los datos de Liga lo respaldan. El Real Madrid solo ha dejado su portería a cero en uno de siete partidos, con 18 goles a favor y 8 en contra. Sus últimos cinco encuentros dejan goles en las dos porterías en tres ocasiones: 4-1 al Rayo, 2-3 en Elche y 1-2 ante el Atlético. El Villarreal, por su parte, ha marcado en cuatro de sus últimos cinco partidos y es un equipo permeable, con 12 goles encajados en siete jornadas. Solo el Alavés lo dejó sin marcar en este tramo. Betfair paga el sí a 1.45, por 2.5 del caso contrario Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles apunta claramente a un partido abierto. Ambos equipos promedian más de 1.7 goles encajados y marcados por encuentro. El Real Madrid acumula 26 tantos entre los suyos y los de sus rivales, y el Villarreal, 25. En los cinco últimos partidos de cada uno, el más de 2.5 goles se ha cumplido en cuatro ocasiones, tanto para los blancos (4-0 al Málaga, 4-1 al Rayo, 2-3 en Elche y 1-2 ante el Atlético) como para el equipo castellonense (2-3 ante el Deportivo, 1-2 ante el Betis, 1-3 en Málaga y 3-1 al Levante). Solo los 1-0 ante Betis y Alavés se quedaron cortos. Betfair sitúa el más de 3.5 goles a 1.68, por 2.1 del caso contrario. Ganar ambas partes El mercado de ganar ambas partes, es decir, que un equipo se imponga tanto en la primera mitad como en la segunda, se presenta como una opción de más riesgo pero con buen potencial para el Real Madrid. El equipo blanco ha firmado goleadas en casa esta temporada (4-0 al Málaga y 4-1 al Rayo) y el Villarreal llega con una defensa vulnerable, que ha encajado en cinco de sus últimos siete partidos de Liga. Si los de Chamartín logran adelantarse pronto y mantener la intensidad tras el descanso, esta apuesta ofrece valor frente al 1X2. Ahora bien, el Villarreal ha sido capaz de marcar en casi todas sus salidas, así que no conviene descartar un partido de alternativas. Betfair paga la victoria del Real Madrid en ambas partes a 2.7.

articles.title: Oregons' Dylan Raiola To Make First Start For Ducks Against No. 21 UCLA
articles.summary: Although quarterback Dante Moore returned to practice, he remains in the concussion protocol, giving quarterback Dylan Raiola his first start for No. 13 Oregon against No. 21 UCLA.
articles.body: Quarterback Dante Moore returned to practice with No. 13 Oregon this week, but he remains in the concussion protocol and won't play on Saturday when the Ducks host No. 21 UCLA. Moore sustained the concussion in a late hit by linebacker Desman Stephens during the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 victory over Southern California on Sept. 26. Moore was placed on a stretcher and left the game in an ambulance. Oregon backup Dylan Raiola took over and threw for 289 yards and two touchdowns against the Trojans. Raiola will get the nod again for the Ducks (3-1, 1-0 Big 10) on Saturday against the No. 21 Bruins (4-0, 2-0) at Autzen Stadium. "He had an expectation when he stepped out there on the field and performed at a really, really high level, and everybody had confidence in him because they see him do it a lot in practice," Oregon coach Dan Lanning said about Raiola. "You get a lot of reps in practice, regardless of where you’re sitting." Raiola transferred to Oregon after starting two seasons at Nebraska, knowing Moore was likely the starter. He has thrown for 413 yards with five touchdowns and no interceptions in two appearances this season. Saturday will be his first start for the Ducks. "It’s totally different systems than what he was running before, so I think you got to build confidence in the system, and that takes time, especially when you ask the quarterback to do as much as we ask the quarterback to do," Lanning said. "You know, whether it’s checks on plays or just the length of a call, right? It’s a little bit different. There’s a lot of variables in there, and it takes some time to get comfortable with it, even when you’re really cerebral and intelligent like Dylan is." UCLA coach Bob Chesney said Moore and Raiola are similar quarterbacks. "They’re both very, very good football players. You can’t really think one way or the other who’s going to be out there and who’s not," Chesney said. "We've got to prepare for both. But really, the good thing is that it’s not like the second kid can’t throw and is only a runner and has to change everything we’re doing." The Ducks have already turned the page from the USC game and everything that came with it, from the worry over Moore's condition to the joy in the victory, Raiola said. "Ultimately, the end of the day, our goal is to win and go 1-0 that week. Very proud of how we fought through the ups and the downs and the moments of that game, we came out on the other side strong, Raiola said. "But on the flip side, kind of put that game to bed last week and been preparing because we've got got a really, really good football team coming to town." While Moore has returned to practice, he was listed on the league’s availability report as out for Saturday and still must complete several benchmarks before he can play in a game. But the team was boosted by his return to practice, even if it was in a limited capacity. "I think the biggest thing is just being able to see a smile on his face to get around and be around his teammates and his brothers and do that at a high level," Lanning said. "Everybody has a smile on their face getting to see Dante out there with us this week, and it’s been fun seeing him compete." articles.title: Tom Brady Remembers The Saddest Moment Of Career: 'Worst Thing I Could've Ever Imagined'
articles.summary: Tom Brady took a painful walk down memory lane in the latest edition of #AskTom.
articles.body: The controversy surrounding a pair of NFL referees getting suspended due to their conduct toward players this past week led Tom Brady to take a bad trip down memory lane, but not in the way you might think. In the most recent edition of #AskTom, Brady was asked what the worst thing he ever heard a ref say during his playing days. His answer wasn't a message that a referee personally gave him. Rather, it was a call that led to arguably the worst loss of Brady's career. "This one’s a little easier than I thought: ‘The catch on the field has been confirmed’ on the David Tyree catch," Brady said, referring to Tyree's remarkable reception in the New York Giants' upset win over the New England Patriots in Super Bowl XLII. "That was the worst thing I could’ve ever imagined." The Tyree catch is arguably the greatest catch in NFL history. With the Giants trailing 14-10 in the final minutes, Eli Manning somehow ran his way out of a sack before completing a 32-yard pass to Tyree, who pinned the ball to his helmet to complete the catch. Four plays later, the Giants scored the game-winning touchdown, ruining the Patriots' chances to become the first team to go 19-0 in NFL history. Nearly 20 years later, Brady remained upset over the play. "We had one of the greatest defenders in Patriots history, Rodney Harrison, covering him," Brady said. "I thought, ‘There’s no way the ball’s getting caught.’ And if it was deflected, there were probably three or four Patriots that were there to catch the ball. "Instead, he pins it against his helmet. And, as he’s falling to the ground, it never comes loose and it ends up being one of the saddest moments in my career." And the catch wasn't the only thing Brady was upset about from that play, either. "Richard Seymour got held; I don’t want to bring that up right now," Brady said, believing that the Giants got away with a holding penalty at the line of scrimmage. Reliving his pain from Super Bowl XLII wasn't the only thing Brady touched on in the latest edition of #AskTom. Brady shared what caused his mishap in the broadcast booth during Sunday's Los Angeles Rams-Philadelphia Eagles game, which player was the best trash talker he's played against and which NBA player he'd like to see play in the NFL. Here's everything Brady said in this week's #AskTom. What’s going on in that giant book that you put on the mute button in the booth? Do you watch film to put that whole thing together? Brady: It is endless amounts of information — six days of preparation: statistics, profiles, how I think the game’s going to be won, the strengths and weaknesses of each team, statistical anomalies and everything under the season. And guess what? I probably get to about 2% during the game. I always look back and go, "God, I had such a good point to make." You’d be surprised, for a three-hour broadcast, how little of the prep I actually use. It’s actually a little bit frustrating. But it’s heavy enough that it can mute you for a good five seconds, huh? Brady: I actually had the very heavy book, set it down and hit the mute TalkBack button. Then, I immediately went into a panic because I couldn’t hear myself. I was scrambling. I threw my headset off. Then, Kevin [Burkhardt] gave me another headset. Put that on. Couldn’t hear that, either. Then, our sound engineer, Ben, came over and said, "Tom, you hit the TalkBack button." And there’s a big red button on my key panel. I was a bit embarrassed. I said, "You know what? It’s like a quarterback fumbling a snap. Let’s just get to the next play." One column I’ve added just recently: I’ve got my list of enemies of which I want to exact revenge from. That’s where that Buffalo comment came from. Who was the best trash talker you’ve ever played against? Brady: There were a few back in the day. Ray Lewis was the most intimidating trash talker because the scary part about Ray was that he could back it all up. So, he was physical, tough, demanding and smart. When he came after you and told you he was going to do something to you, he usually did. It was kind of scary. One who was a little annoying at first, but became a teammate, was Richard Sherman. The first time I played against him, it was in Seattle, and we went through the whole game. He makes some comment to me at the end of the third quarter, I think he and Earl Thomas. And then, I really didn’t know what they said. It was so loud in the stadium. They were talking. I think they were hyped up. I may have said a few things back. After the game, they came up and I thought they came up to shake hands and be good sportsmen. It turns out, they actually didn’t. So, Sherm, I’m glad I got to be your buddy and teammate. We’ve hashed it out. So, we’re great. One other annoying trash talker? Rex Ryan. Guess who couldn’t back it up? Rex Ryan and the Jets all those years. Rex, just shut up. You had terrible teams. You were a terrible trash talker. He’s on that revenge column in the book, right? Brady: I got my revenge when I played against him. I didn’t need to get it post-career. What was the worst thing that you ever heard come out of a ref’s mouth? Brady: This one’s a little easier than I thought: "The catch on the field has been confirmed" on the David Tyree catch. That was the worst thing I could’ve ever imagined. Do you remember seeing that? Was the jumbotron in that stadium big enough that you knew what was coming? Brady: I actually got a good view of it, and the ball was sort of floating down. It was kind of a wobbler. Eli [Manning] escaped the traffic — Richard Seymour got held; I don’t want to bring that up right now. It’s still a little bit of a sore subject. Eli floats it down the middle to David Tyree and I think it was kind of a Hail Mary. We had one of the greatest defenders in Patriots history, Rodney Harrison, covering him. I thought, "There’s no way the ball’s getting caught." And if it was deflected, there were probably three or four Patriots that were there to catch the ball. Instead, he pins it against his helmet. And, as he’s falling to the ground, it never comes loose and it ends up being one of the saddest moments in my career. What do you say to all the fans that Brady started the crying-to-the-refs debacle we’ve got going on now? Brady: Listen, I never cried to the refs, b---es. Don’t talk s--- to me. I’ve got the microphone, and I can talk back. Are there drills to improve pocket presence? How would you coach a young QB who has some of these escaping problems that you talk about? Brady: A lot of it, I think, can be drilled. I think part of it is being aware where the soft spot in the pocket is. For a quarterback that’s not really going to run outside the pocket right or left or escape around the tackle, there’s always a nice firm spot in the pocket between the two guard spots. At that point, you’re just working to find space. To me, it was always about being on the balls of your feet, but also setting up a lot of cone drills where you shuffle right, shuffle left and shuffle left, shuffle right. As a quarterback, you should never go back in the pocket. To me, it was always, right, left and up and continue to stay on the ball of your feet looking for the soft spot. Coaches would throw bean bags at our feet. They would swipe at us as we ducked underneath bags. They would throw weighted towels at us. Anything to distract us while feeling the pocket through our peripheral vision, but maintaining our eyes downfield. A lot of guys, it feels like, are running too early these days. Who is somebody who does a good job in the pocket right now? Brady: I think Patrick Mahomes does a great job, knowing when to run, stay in the pocket and deliver the football. I know it doesn’t look pretty, but throwing a ball 20 yards down the field and completing a pass sometimes can look effortless when you can have a dynamic 12-yard run. But, at the end of the day, the game is points and it’s about production and yards. Obviously, the more yards you gain per play, the more successful you’re going to be. So, a 20-yard throw can look relatively simple, it can be way more effective than a short run. Look, I’m all for escapability. I think it’s a great tool to have. I just think you’ve got to use it at the right time and at an appropriate time for your team. Are there tells that defensive backs watch for like "patting" the football? Did you ever have to think about this or change anything in your delivery? Brady: I always thought patting the football was a rhythm thing. I never really saw it as a detriment. I think the thought is from the time the quarterback decides to throw to the time the ball hits the receiver's hands; that’s the timeframe that needs to be as quick as possible. If it’s an elaborated patt and it’s a little slow, then you have a problem. It’s just as if you’re making your decision for the rhythm of the throw that it doesn’t slow you down as much as you think. I don’t think the DB can get a beat on it before it gets to the receiver’s hands. So, I think the patt’s a little bit overrated. Good fundamentals and an accurate throw with the appropriate amount of pace are what matters most. I think the DBs are always looking at the shoulders of the quarterback and which direction he’s pointing the shoulder in for them to break on the ball. You can put one current NBA player onto an NFL team right now. Who is it, what team and what position? Brady: I’m putting LeBron James on the Las Vegas Raiders. At the end of the day, he’s the right age. He’s got the experience. He’s got the height. He’s a prolific scorer. Get him down in the red zone, run a little flag route, send him out wide, give him a slant or a fade and let him go high-point the ball. I’ve seen his head go above the rim. This is the easiest touchdown we could ever throw. It’s just throwing it up to LeBron. FOX SPORTS NEWSLETTERYour teams. Your sports. articles.title: La emotiva despedida de Gustavo Oliva, figura clave en el crecimiento del pádel en España: "Irte con 58 años es pronto"
articles.standfirst: Una de las personas que más ha trabajado por el crecimiento del pádel, diagnosticado de cáncer, ha querido compartir varias reflexiones sobre la vida, la familia y la prevención
articles.summary: Una de las personas que más ha trabajado por el crecimiento del pádel, diagnosticado de cáncer, ha querido compartir varias reflexiones sobre la vida, la familia y la prevención
articles.body: Gustavo Oliva, una figura vinculada durante décadas al crecimiento del pádel en España, ha publicado un mensaje de despedida mientras continúa librando una larga lucha contra el cáncer. A sus 58 años, el catalán explica que su vida "en la Tierra llega a su fin en breve" y aprovecha el mensaje para agradecer el apoyo recibido y concienciar sobre la importancia de la prevención y las revisiones médicas. Oliva fue diagnosticado a finales de 2023 de un cáncer colorrectal que ya presentaba metástasis. Según explica en su mensaje, la enfermedad se había extendido al hígado, el bazo y numerosos ganglios. El jugador reconoce que llevaba una vida saludable, pero admite que no prestó suficiente atención a las revisiones preventivas. "Siguiendo la prevención aconsejada, seguro que se hubiera detectado a tiempo", señala. Su trayectoria está estrechamente ligada al desarrollo del pádel. Jugador durante más de 25 años, llegó a estar entre los 50 mejores de España y los diez mejores de Cataluña, además de ejercer como capitán de la selección catalana entre 2014 y 2017. También fue responsable de marketing en ASICS y participó desde la industria deportiva en el desarrollo y promoción del pádel, además de impulsar proyectos de formación a través de Padel Academy Barcelona. En su escrito, Oliva hace balance de su vida y de los últimos años, y destaca especialmente el apoyo de su familia y sus amigos. "Irte con 58 años en nuestros tiempos y nuestro entorno es pronto", afirma. Su mensaje ha provocado numerosas muestras de cariño dentro del mundo del pádel, donde es conocido tanto por su trayectoria como jugador como por su trabajo en la formación y en la promoción de este deporte. "He tenido la suerte de tener una vida llena de salud, sin ningún contratiempo importante y pudiendo disfrutar al máximo en cada momento. Quizás por ello y exceso de confianza no seguí unas normas básicas de prevención, y cuando empecé a notar los primeros síntomas, ya tenía un enorme cáncer colorrectal con metástasis en hígado, bazo y numerosos ganglios. Siguiendo la prevención aconsejada, seguro que se hubiera detectado a tiempo", explica, antes de despedirse: "Hasta siempre familia. Hasta siempre amigos".

articles.title: A’ja Wilson wins her third straight WNBA MVP and record fifth overall
articles.summary: Former US Vice President Kamala Harris among those to hail Wilson as Las Vegas Aces centre continues record run.
articles.body:
A’ja Wilson fine-tunes her shooting touch after every practice. That extra work has defined her greatness since being drafted first overall in 2018.

On Thursday, she received a voice message from former Vice President Kamala Harris congratulating her on redefining greatness leaguewide after she was named the WNBA’s MVP for a third straight year and for the fifth time overall.

“Obviously, that is an honour,” Wilson said. “A woman of our history, and I’m so appreciative to be able to share that moment with her through the phone call and the message of her delivering that I won my fifth MVP.”

In addition to becoming the first player to three-peat, Wilson won the award in 2020 and 2022.

Commissioner Cathy Engelbert, Aces owner Mark Davis and team President Nikki Fargas accompanied Wilson’s mother, Eva, who presented her daughter with the trophy.

“Each one of these has not been taken lightly,” Wilson said while flanked by all five of her MVP trophies. “In my heart, they’ve always been so special. But this one here, I cried a little bit harder. This one here is just a little bit different. … When you dream as a young girl, you dream so big and you write your goals out, and you just never imagine that you were able to just check them off.

“And when you’re able to check them off – small wins, big wins – it truly means a lot. And so I think that’s why I cried a little bit harder on this one, because 15-year-old A’ja wasn’t sitting up here dreaming about being a five-time MVP. She wasn’t dreaming about being a three-time champion. She was dreaming about surviving this world.”

The 30-year-old Wilson once again led the league in scoring with an average of 26.2 points per game while shooting nearly 53 percent from the field. She averaged 9.4 rebounds per game, a career-best 3.2 assists and 1.9 blocks.

Wilson has the defending champion Aces back in the WNBA semifinals for the eighth consecutive season although Las Vegas is down 2-0 in the best-of-five series against Golden State. Game 3 is on Friday.

“This is great. I love it, not going to take for granted, shine her up, let’s do it,” Wilson said on Thursday. “But tomorrow, when it comes to hoisting it in front of the fans, I love the fans, … but I doubt I will be doing that. I’ll be warming up with my team. … Everyone in this room knows the competitor that I am. Everyone knows what my main focus is, and that is to get a game.”

Wilson received 65 first-place votes and nine second-place votes for a total of 713 points from a national panel of sportswriters and broadcasters. Minnesota’s Olivia Miles received six first-place votes and 40 second-place votes (442 points) while Indiana guards Kelsey Mitchell and Caitlin Clark followed with 287 and 212 points, respectively.

No WNBA player besides Wilson has more than three MVPs. Sheryl Swoopes, Lisa Leslie and Lauren Jackson each have a trio. On the NBA side, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar has six, and Michael Jordan and Bill Russell each have five.

“A’ja Wilson is one of one,” Fargas said. “She’s now standing in a category that no other WNBA player in the history of the league has accomplished. She’s in the conversations with the Michael Jordans and the Wayne Gretzkys of the world – where she belongs.”

articles.title: "Somos tenistas, y punto": De la Puente y Caverzaschi, con McEnroe, Sabatini y la Fundación Sanitas
articles.standfirst: Cientos de espectadores asistieron al I Masters de Tenis Inclusivo
articles.summary: Cientos de espectadores asistieron al I Masters de Tenis Inclusivo
articles.body: El tenis tiene distintas modalidades pero es un solo deporte. Quedó ayer patente una vez más en el Estadio 3 de la Caja Mágica durante el I Masters de Tenis Inclusivo auspiciado por la Fundación Sanitas. Leyendas del deporte de la raqueta como John McEnroe y Gabriela Sabatini, la colaboración de Alex Corretja, dos líderes mundiales del tenis en silla de ruedas como Dani Carverzaschi y Martín de la Puente, jugadores de tenis adaptado en pie como Thalita Rodrigues e Iván Corretja y otros tenistas en silla como Laura Sambruno, Carmen Lobo y Sam Gómez brindaron un espectáculo seguido en directo por centenares de espectadores. Los protagonistas actuaron divididos en dos equipos, capitaneados por McEnroe y Sabatini, que también saltaron a la pista para disputar dobles junto a los 'adaptados en pie' y los dos líderes, Dani y Martín. Más importante en este caso que el resultado en sí fue el hecho de que se aplicó un reglamento oficial de tenis inclusivo, desarrollado por Fundación Sanitas, expertos en tenis convencional y adaptado y la Cátedra Fundación Sanitas de Deporte Inclusivo de la Universidad Politécnica de Madrid. Se analizaron características de cada modalidad y definido las adaptaciones necesarias para favorecer la igualdad de condiciones. En para que tenistas con y sin discapacidad pudieran competir en igualdad de oportunidades. Carlos Jaureguízar, CEO de Sanitas y de Bupa Europe & LatinAmerica y presidente de Fundación Sanitas, señaló que "volvemos a ser pioneros y demostrar que el deporte del futuro será inclusivo. Porque esa es la esencia de nuestro trabajo, conseguir que las personas con y sin discapacidad disfruten de una misma forma de competir”. John McEnroe, 'Supermac', destacó el esfuerzo y la entrega de los tenistas en silla y Sabatini, que esta iniciativa sirve para tomar conciencia de la importancia y el alcance del deporte adaptado: "es un honor compartir una cancha de tenis con Martín de la Puente, con Dani Caverzaschi y los demás". Y el hecho es que Dani y Martín han compartido de forma muy principal el protagonismo con McEnroe y Sabatini. Su protagonismo social creció exponencialmente con su medalla de bronce en dobles los Juegos Paralímpicos de París 2024. Pero a ellos lo que más les satisface es que, en efecto, ha podido ser un punto de partida: "Creo que fue buena cosa, para el tenis en silla y para el tenis español en general -dice Martín- Notamos que tenemos más presencia pero creemos que hay que seguir, que esto no es solo para que Martín y Dani salgan en más fotos: es para que chicos tengan más oportunidades para jugar. Creo que estamos en el buen camino pero tenemos que seguir construyendo algo bonito para dar oportunidades a los chicos, que son los que se lo merecen". Dani cree que este camino hacia el progreso en el tenis en silla "hay que abordarlos desde distintos puntos de vista. Ese día de la medalla nos vieron muchos, y vieron un partido emocionante, súper tenso y bonito. Y tomándolo desde la base, puede servir que lo vea alguien que prueba el tenis en silla por primera vez y piensa que ojalá algún día sea élite. Es una pirámide e iniciativas como estas están muy bien para ello". Y el tenis en silla está, además, ganando un importante espacio competitivo con un circuito internacional consolidado e importante presencia en los cuatro torneos de Grand Slam. "Estando en los sitios donde se juega el tenis de más élite demostramos que hay oportunidades para todos. Es importante: Dani y yo -dice Martín- hemos jugado en pistas viéndonos nuestra familia y nuestro entrenador, entrenando a solas con la lluvia y el sol. Y que te venga a ver gente y conozca el tenis en silla creo que es la mayor victoria que podemos conseguir. Además, Dani y yo tenemos una rivalidad muy bonita que hace que crezca el nivel del tenis en silla en España. Y es importante mostrarlo en los grandes escenarios". Además, en estos torneos los grandes del tenis en silla entran en contacto con las grandes estrellas mundiales del tenis 'en pie'. "Los profesionales se acercan cada vez más a nosotros -dice Dani- Martín y yo tenemos grandes amigos dentro del circuito. Y son compañeros de profesión que nos respetan como tenistas, más allá de decir 'mira, vienen los de la silla'. No, nos ven entrenar y dicen 'estos tíos se matan y juegan bien. Creo que se nos respeta y se nos considera como profesionales, que siempre fue lo que Martín y yo queríamos, olvidar diferencias porque más allá de la discapacidad, somos tenistas, y punto". "Y los medios son importantes en esto -señala Martín- Estamos muy agradecidos por su trabajo y la visibilidad que nos dais. Lo agradecemos mucho".

articles.title: ‘I was a daughter of Himachal’: Ritu Negi’s heartbreak after home state drops Asian Games gold medallist from Rs 1 crore reward list
articles.summary: Former India captain Ritu Negi has represented the country at three consecutive Asian Games, won two gold medals and a silver, and led the women's kabaddi
articles.body: Former India captain Ritu Negi has represented the country at three consecutive Asian Games, won two gold medals and a silver, and led the women's kabaddi team to the top of the podium at the 2023 edition in Hangzhou. Yet, after being part of India's gold-medal-winning squad again at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, the Arjuna Awardee has found herself at the centre of an unexpected controversy in her home state of Himachal Pradesh.Negi's name was missing from the state's list of athletes announced for a cash reward of Rs 1 crore following India's women's kabaddi triumph in Japan. The decision has left the veteran player disappointed and raised questions about whether an accomplished sportsperson should lose recognition from her home state simply because she is married in another state.Negi hails from the Shillai region of Sirmaur district but is married in Panipat, Haryana. The omission has been particularly difficult to understand because she received a cash reward from Himachal Pradesh after India's women's kabaddi team won gold at the 2023 Asian Games, when she was the captain.This time, however, her name was left out while three other players from the state were included in the reward list."Until a week ago, I was a daughter of Himachal and the CM shared a congratulatory message on Facebook, while former CM Jairam Thakur and Member of Parliament Anurag Thakur had called to congratulate me," Negi told the media while expressing her displeasure."I simply cannot understand what changed so suddenly two days ago."‘Why is Himachal Pradesh behaving this way at this stage of my career?’The decision to exclude Negi has struck a particularly sensitive chord because of her long association with Indian kabaddi and her contribution to the state's sporting reputation.The veteran has represented India at three consecutive Asian Games, winning two gold medals and a silver. She captained the women's team to gold at Hangzhou in 2023 and remained part of the squad that successfully defended the title in Japan.India edged past Iran 37-34 in a tense final at the Aichi-Nagoya Games, holding on to its advantage in the closing stages to secure another Asian Games gold.The achievement should have been another moment of pride for the player and her home state. Instead, the omission from the reward list has left Negi questioning the recognition being extended to her.She pointed out that although she is employed by Indian Railways, she has consistently represented Himachal Pradesh, rather than Haryana, in domestic competitions."Why Himachal Pradesh is behaving in such a way at this stage of my career?" she asked.For Negi, the issue goes beyond the financial incentive. It is about recognition for years of representing India and maintaining her sporting association with the state from which she hails.Her father asks: Does a daughter stop belonging to her state after marriage?Negi's father, Bhavan Singh Negi, has also questioned the decision, asking whether a daughter ceases to belong to her home state simply because she gets married elsewhere.Speaking from Shillai in Sirmaur district, he pointed out that his daughter had received a cash reward from the Himachal government after the 2023 Asian Games, despite being married in Haryana.That precedent has made the latest omission even harder for the family to comprehend. They believe marriage should not erase an athlete's roots or diminish her contribution to the state she continues to represent in domestic competitions.The controversy has since drawn reactions from political leaders and people associated with sports in Himachal Pradesh.The debate has consequently become about more than a reward announced after a sporting achievement. It has raised questions about how states recognise athletes who continue to bring them distinction despite changes in their personal circumstances.Why three kabaddi players were awarded Rs 1 crore eachThe controversy emerged after Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu announced a cash reward of Rs 1 crore each for three players from the state who were part of India's women's kabaddi gold-medal-winning squad at the Aichi-Nagoya Games.The recipients were Pushpa Rana, Jyoti Thakur and Bhawna Thakur. Indian women's cricket player Renuka Thakur was also announced as a recipient of Rs 1 crore in recognition of her achievements.The announcement followed an earlier disagreement over the amount offered to the kabaddi players. Initially, the three players had been informed that they would receive Rs 33 lakh each, a figure they felt was below their entitlement under the state's sports policy. They subsequently met Sukhu to raise their concerns over the cash incentives and employment opportunities.Pushpa Rana said the players were disappointed by the original announcement."Look, we were very disappointed because according to the sports policy, we were not being given the amount that was due to us. So literally, anyone would be disappointed," she told IANS.Following the meeting, the Chief Minister assured the players that the reward would be increased to Rs 1 crore each. The state government also announced government employment for the three kabaddi players, with options in the police department or the Youth Services and Sports Department.While the revised announcement addressed the players' concerns over the amount, Negi's omission from the list brought a fresh controversy into focus.Government promises to review the decisionThe Himachal Pradesh government has not publicly provided a definitive explanation for why Negi's name was removed from the list.Sports Minister Yadvinder Goma said he was unaware of the reason behind the change and would examine the file before discussing the matter with the Chief Minister.Meanwhile, sources in the state government indicated that officials were monitoring the Haryana government's position on the matter. They suggested that Himachal Pradesh could consider a decision later, particularly since Haryana had not yet announced a cash award for Negi.The sources also indicated that her employment with Indian Railways was not a factor in the matter.The distinction is important because Negi has maintained that she has continued to represent Himachal Pradesh in domestic competitions despite her marriage and employment outside the state.Whether the government ultimately revises its list remains to be seen. For now, the Sports Minister's assurance that he will review the matter offers a possible route towards resolving the dispute.Another gold medal, but a different kind of disappointmentFor Negi, the timing of the controversy is especially poignant.At the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou, she captained the women's kabaddi side to gold and received recognition from her home state. At the Aichi-Nagoya Games, she again stood among the Indian players who helped defend the title, contributing to a campaign that ended with another gold medal for the country.Her sporting journey has been built around representing India at the highest level while continuing to identify with Himachal Pradesh. The latest controversy has placed that connection under an uncomfortable spotlight.Negi's case also highlights a broader challenge in Indian sport: ensuring that recognition for athletes reflects their achievements and contributions, rather than becoming entangled in questions about residence, marriage or administrative eligibility.The government has yet to make its final position clear, and the possibility of reconsideration remains open. articles.title: Final Picks for Roman Reigns vs. LA Knight and WWE Money in the Bank 2026 Match Card
articles.summary: This Saturday, the annual Money in the Bank PLE finally arrives. As one of the more exciting WWE events on the calendar, a lot of eyes will be on the company this weekend.
articles.body:
This Saturday, the annual Money in the Bank PLE finally arrives. As one of the more exciting WWE events on the calendar, a lot of eyes will be on the company this weekend.

The two titular ladder matches for the men's and women's Money in the Bank briefcases have a mix of former and future world champions, so we should be in for a good show.

In addition to Roman Reigns and Stephanie Vaquer defending their respective world titles, we will also see Oba Femi battle Bronson Reed.

Let's go through each match on the card and make some predictions.

At this point, it feels like WWE is just trying to keep Femi busy, possibly until the Royal Rumble where he will make his ascent, but Bronson Reed is certainly somebody who is not to be overlooked.

Reed recently returned from an injury with a slimmer physique and the same old intensity. It feels like WWE might want to give him a sustained push this time.

However, Femi is the priority. He defeated Brock Lesnar twice this year, and he bested Bron Breakker after that. He is on a roll, and it's not going to slow down anytime soon.

This will be a great fight between two powerhouse performers, but The Ruler is going to overcome The Vision once again and claim the win.

Stephanie Vaquer vs. Liv Morgan vs. Becky Lynch

Stephanie Vaquer will defend the women's world title against Liv Morgan and Becky Lynch this weekend, and while the champion will likely retain in that match, this also feels like a possible place for a cash-in attempt.

WWE usually spaces the two MITB bouts out so one begins the night, and the other ends it. The women's bout usually ends up being the first, so it opens the door for a same-night cash-in.

Vaquer will successfully fend off Morgan and Lynch, but whether someone successfully cashes in is the real question.

While it would be great to see LA Knight get the upset victory and win his first world title in WWE, it's not gonna happen this weekend.

This feud simply hasn't been built up to make it seem like dethroning Reigns is a realistic option.

The OTC is WWE's golden boy. He has been portrayed as someone who is only beaten when the time is right, and sadly for Knight, that time is not on Saturday.

This will be a fun match, and The Megastar will come close several times, but Reigns will beat him and continue his reign as the men's world champion heading into 2027.

The field for this year's women's MITB bout includes Sol Ruca, Lola Vice, Jacy Jayne, Roxanne Perez, Lash Legend and Tiffany Stratton.

Tiffy has won the briefcase before, Jayne is the current United States champion, and Vice is still very new on the main roster, so we are ruling them out right away.

Legend and Ruca would both be reasonable options, but this feels like the perfect time to give Perez the push she has been waiting for since she arrived on the main roster.

Morgan has had her time as the world champion, and Rodriguez is still in the midst of her reign as the IC champion, so giving Perez the briefcase will elevate her to their level in Judgment Day.

This year's men's MITB match includes Bron Breakker, Je'Von Evans, Trick Williams, Penta, CM Punk and Kevin Owens. Punk and Owens are the only former world champions in the match, so there is a lot of potential for one of the other four men to break into the main event scene as a result of this bout.

Williams will definitely be challenging for world titles someday, and so will Evans. Penta just had his first opportunity against Reigns in Mexico, but he came up short.

Out of everyone listed, Breakker feels like the most obvious candidate to win. He did his job and put Femi over, and now it's time for him to have his moment.

The Vision already holds the tag titles on Raw, so adding the MITB briefcase will give the group even more momentum as we head into the end of the year.

articles.title: The Argument For These 2 WWE Stars Winning Money in the Bank Ladder Matches
articles.summary: WWE Money in the Bank is this weekend, and the field is set for two decidedly different ladder matches.
articles.body:
WWE Money in the Bank is this weekend, and the field is set for two decidedly different ladder matches.

On the men's side, most of the participants have already set their sights on Sami Zayn and the Undisputed WWE Championship. Meanwhile, Bron Breakker is desperate to prove he can eclipse Oba Femi as the next top star.

A win on Saturday would erase his 2026 struggles and give him a chance to pull a page out of his mentor's playbook. Although Seth Rollins became his bitter rival, The Visionary famously affirmed what the Money in the Bank briefcase could do for his career.

Conversely, many of the women are relatively new to this stipulation match. This gives Tiffany Stratton, the 2024 winner, a slight advantage, but anyone could climb the ladder to earn the opportunity of a lifetime.

According to MyBookie , Roxanne Perez is the favorite to win the women's ladder match, and Breakker is favored to win the men's. Here's our case for both young participants to finally step into the spotlight this year.

Roxanne Perez Must Leave The Judgment Day

Ever since WWE signed Perez in 2022, she has been earmarked as a future Superstar. The Prodigy stood out in Ring of Honor's fledgling women's division before Tony Khan purchased the company around the same time.

As such, the inaugural ROH Women's World Champion was a major acquisition because she would've been an asset to the promotion under Khan. Her heel run on NXT confirmed that the 24-year-old was more than just a great in-ring performer.

Perez topped many year-end lists in 2024 as a lynchpin for the developmental brand. Initially, her inevitable jump to the main roster was promising because she excelled in multi-woman matches against some of the brightest stars.

However, it's hard to deny that she lost some momentum as a member of The Judgment Day. The stable has outlived its usefulness, and most of its members would be better off if it ultimately imploded.

WWE has been teasing a split for so long, and the Money in the Bank contract could finally give Perez the means to break off on her own. She has had tension with Liv Morgan since the group ousted Finn Bálor in March.

It's time to pay off that lingering plot thread in an interesting way. Even more, the company's main title picture could use a reset, and this is the perfect time to see if Perez can live up to the hype.

2026 has been a tough year for Breakker. Most of us expected his turn on Rollins to culminate in a crowning moment, but that never materialized.

Even worse, his Royal Rumble appearance lasted 10 seconds, and the storyline didn't even lead to a match at WrestleMania 42. Although Breakker defeated his former mentor at Backlash, their feud didn't elevate him as many expected.

Their steel cage match at Night of Champions was strong. However, it kind of came and went, and Rollins quickly moved on to a highly anticipated showdown with Roman Reigns at SummerSlam.

It certainly didn't help that Femi emerged as the future of the company after his trilogy of matches with Brock Lesnar. In a matter of months, The Ruler has become a fan favorite and shot ahead of him in the pecking order.

This is a bit baffling because WWE has positioned Breakker as the next big thing since his debut on NXT 2.0. When he betrayed Rollins last year, that seemed to signal that the company was ready to push him into the main event scene.

Instead, the creative team has taken several half-measures with him that left us scratching our heads. The men's Money in the Bank ladder match provides the latest attempt to guess whether he will leap to the next level or languish in The Vision.

The problem is Penta is hotter right now due to his world heavyweight championship match with Reigns in Mexico City. Kevin Owens is also a much more interesting option because of his history with Zayn, and he is long overdue for another world title run.

Still, Breakker needs this win more than the two of them. The 28-year-old must find a way to salvage this year and put himself in the same conversation with Femi.

He didn't make an impact at Royal Rumble, and he didn't compete in the King of the Ring tournament. It's now or never for "The Unpredictable Badass".

articles.title: BS Meter on Dylan Larkin, Connor Hellebuyck, Simon Edvinsson and the Latest NHL Trade Rumors
articles.summary: It's been over a week since the puck dropped on the 2026-27 NHL regular season. As the 32 teams begin the long quest to determine the next Stanley Cup champion, the rumor mill is churning.
articles.body:
It's been over a week since the puck dropped on the 2026-27 NHL regular season. As the 32 teams begin the long quest to determine the next Stanley Cup champion, the rumor mill is churning.

The buzz increased following the blockbuster trade on Sept. 28, in which the Columbus Blue Jackets shipped winger Kirill Marchenko to the Toronto Maple Leafs for power forward Matthew Knies in a six-player swap .

That's sparked renewed speculation about several notable stars who've been considered trade candidates since the offseason. Some of them, like Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin and Winnipeg Jets goaltender Connor Hellebuyck, regularly appeared on our NHL Trade Boards .

Several other players also surfaced in the rumor mill. Among them is Larkin's teammate Simon Edvinsson, who's returned to Sweden to await a new contract or a trade.

Could these players be moved anytime soon? Follow along as we dust off our trusty BS Meter to determine fact from fiction.

Could the Calgary Flames Sign a Free-Agent Forward to Bolster Their Scoring?

It was a disastrous opening week for the Calgary Flames. Outscored 16-3 in their first three games, they were last in the overall standings with the worst goals-per-game average (1.00) and the highest goals-against-per-game average (5.33).

Having traded away most of their veteran scorers, the rebuilding Flames are in desperate need of an offensive boost if they're to be competitive this season. That could send them into what's left of this year's thin free-agent market for help.

On Oct. 6, TSN's Pierre LeBrun reported that the Flames "kicked around" the possibility of signing Patrik Laine. Injuries have hampered the 28-year-old winger in recent years, but when healthy, he'd be an affordable 20-goal scorer.

The following day, Sportsnet's Frank Servalli reported that Laine isn't the only UFA the Flames could consider. He noted that veteran wingers like Vladimir Tarasenko, David Perron, and James van Riemsdyk are still available.

The Flames must not only improve their scoring but also add a veteran who can mentor their promising young scorers. Those veteran UFAs are likely willing to sign with any team at this point. If they play well, they could be flipped to a contender at the March trade deadline for draft picks and prospects.

Has Vancouver Canucks Center Elias Pettersson Improved His Trade Value?

For the past two years, Elias Pettersson has frequently been the subject of NHL trade rumors. The Vancouver Canucks' collapse over the last two seasons, combined with the 27-year-old center's declining production and hefty contract, has earned him a regular spot on our NHL Trade Boards .

It's early in the season, but the now-rebuilding Canucks are off to a decent start. Pettersson has played a key role with a solid two-way game and sits among their leading scorers .

Ben Kuzma of The Vancouver Province suggested Pettersson could be of value to the Canucks if he maintains his performance and helps develop promising young centers like Braeden Cootes and Caleb Malhotra. However, he might also be improving his trade market value.

Sportsnet's Michael Amato also noted Pettersson's opening-week play. He thinks the 27-year-old center's $11.6 million average annual value isn't as burdensome given the sharp rise in player salaries. The lack of quality centers in the trade market could also make him an enticing target.

It'll take more than a solid week of play to convince teams seeking a top-six center that Pettersson's inconsistency is a thing of the past. Furthermore, he has a full no-movement clause and has maintained that he's not interested in a trade.

Only two games into this season, Florida Panthers captain Aleksander Barkov was placed on long-term injury reserve after sustaining a left leg injury against the San Jose Sharks. The 32-year-old center missed all of last season following knee surgery last September.

Some observers believed another lengthy absence for Barkov could force the Panthers to find a replacement, either within their organization or in the trade market. There was speculation that they might look into acquiring center Dylan Larkin from the Detroit Red Wings.

Larkin, 30, requested a trade during the offseason, making him a fixture in this summer's rumor mill. The two-way center was No. 2 on our October NHL Trade Block Big Board . He's signed through 2030-31 with an average annual value of $8.7 million and a full no-movement clause.

The Panthers are on Larkin's list of destinations. During an Oct. 2 appearance on NHL Network, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman said the Panthers had limited trade capital to acquire Larkin. Meanwhile, The Athletic's Eric Stephens questioned whether the cap-strapped Panthers could afford Larkin's contract.

On Oct. 6, the Panthers announced that Barkov was sidelined for six to eight weeks. TSN's Pierre LeBrun believes that should silence the rumors linking Larkin to the Panthers, noting that they wouldn't pursue a replacement for their captain if he's returning within eight weeks.

Players That Will Dominate the Rumor Mill

Connor Hellebuyck to the Edmonton Oilers?

For the past four months, Connor Hellebuyck has been at the top of our NHL Trade Boards . The 33-year-old Winnipeg Jets goaltender made his trade request public in August. He remains suspended without pay by the Jets for failing to report to training camp while he tries to force a trade.

Meanwhile, the porous performance of goaltenders Tristan Jarry and Devon Levi in the club's first two games became an early concern for the Edmonton Oilers. With offseason acquisition Frederik Andersen sidelined until December, there was speculation that they could seek a short-term solution.

On Oct. 1, Sportsnet's Frank Seravalli wondered if the Oilers might make a pitch for Hellebuyck. He mused over whether the three-time Vezina Trophy winner might accept a trade to Edmonton, and whether the Jets might soften their stance on getting a goalie in return for Hellebuyck.

Seravalli acknowledged the stumbling blocks in the path to a trade with Edmonton. Hellebuyck might not want to go to another Canadian team; the Oilers lack the cap space and sufficient tradeable assets, and they could insist on the Jets taking Jarry in return.

Seravalli admitted it's a long shot that Hellebuyck would accept a trade to Edmonton. Too many factors work against that option. On Oct. 6, TSN's Pierre LeBrun said Hellebuyck was " never gonna play in Canada ."

The Detroit Red Wings are already dealing with a player who has wanted a trade since June, when center Dylan Larkin went public with his request. They could have another player who wants out, as Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that the 23-year-old defenseman would prefer a trade.

Edvinsson is a restricted free agent who returned to Sweden to await a new contract with the Red Wings. Negotiations stalled during the summer when Steve Yzerman was removed as general manager, and there are no signs of progress in those discussions with interim GM Shawn Horcoff.

Friedman said neither the Red Wings nor Edvinsson's representatives would confirm that the blueliner wants a trade. He also indicated that the Red Wings' priority is to re-sign him, but later said they've gauged his value on the trade market.

William Espy of The Hockey News believes it would make sense for the San Jose Sharks to acquire Edvinsson. He'd provide a significant boost to the left side of their blue line. However, he would be expensive to acquire and sign.

Sharks' general manager, Mike Grier, isn't afraid to make bold moves. He'd have to give up some promising assets to sign Edvinsson, and it could cost over $10 million annually. Nevertheless, he'd be a terrific addition to the rebuilding Sharks and could bring long-term stability to the left side of their defense corps.

articles.title: Updated 2026 WWE Money in the Bank Card and Predictions for Match Order
articles.summary: The course of WWE history could change Saturday night when many of the company's top Superstars converge on New Orleans for Money in the Bank.
articles.body:
The course of WWE history could change Saturday night when many of the company's top Superstars converge on New Orleans for Money in the Bank.

Two Superstars will leave The Big Easy with guaranteed world title opportunities in tow by virtue of winning the highly anticipated men's and women's Money in the Bank ladder matches.

On top of that, Roman Reigns is set to put the World Heavyweight Championship on the line, and the Women's World Championship will be contested in a Triple Threat match.

Now or Never for LA Knight, More Raw Fallout 🗣️

Here is everything you need to know about Money in the Bank, including a look at the entire card and the projected match order.

Where: Smoothie King Center in New Orleans

Money in the Bank 2026 Card and Projected Match Order

Women's Money in the Bank Ladder Match: Sol Ruca vs. Lola Vice vs. Jacy Jayne vs. Roxanne Perez vs. Lash Legend vs. Tiffany Stratton

Women's World Championship Triple Threat: Stephanie Vaquer (c) vs. Liv Morgan vs. Becky Lynch

Men's Money in the Bank Ladder Match: Bron Breakker vs. Je'Von Evans vs. Trick Williams vs. Penta vs. CM Punk vs. Kevin Owens

World Heavyweight Championship: Roman Reigns (c) vs. LA Knight

Top Money in the Bank 2026 Matches to Watch

One of six men will climb the ladder and secure the Money in the Bank contract on Saturday, giving them a world title shot at a time and place of their choosing.

The field for Saturday's contest is stacked with talent and features plenty of variance in terms of stars on the rise and those who have already been to the mountaintop.

Bron Breakker, Penta, Trick Williams and Je'Von Evans are all searching for a career-defining win that would bring them to within one step of their first WWE or World Heavyweight Championship.

CM Punk and Kevin Owens already know what it's like to be "the guy," but it has been nearly a decade since KO has been in that position, and Punk is looking for a quick route back to the WWE title after shenanigans cost him against Sami Zayn recently.

Penta and Breakker feel like the top candidates to win because they have both come agonizingly close to becoming world champ before, and need one last nudge to put them over the top.

However, Owens can't be counted out either since it has been so long since his first and only world title reign, and because the idea of him tormenting Zayn with the Money in the Bank contract could hypothetically create some highly entertaining programming on SmackDown.

Aside from Tiffany Stratton, every combatant in the women's Money in the Bank ladder match will be vying for a chance to win the WWE women's or women's world title for the first time.

The match features a ton of young talent that has enjoyed success early in their careers, as Sol Ruca, Roxanne Perez, Jacy Jayne and Lola Vice all held major titles in NXT, while Lash Legend is a former WWE women's tag team champion.

Additionally, Jayne is the reigning women's United States champion and Ruca previously held the Women's Intercontinental Championship, which speaks to the idea that they are ready for the next step.

Stratton has the clear experience edge over the rest of the field as a one-time Money in the Bank ladder match winner and WWE women's champion.

It is fair to say that there is no favorite who stands out above the rest, as any of the six Superstars in women's Money in the Bank can make a case for being a deserving and logical winner.

That adds a great deal of intrigue to the bout, as does the fact that so many young, hungry competitors will want to prove their worth on a big stage like MITB.

In the likely main event of Money in the Bank, LA Knight will get another chance to topple Roman Reigns and become a world champion for the first time in WWE.

Knight previously challenged Reigns for the WWE Championship in a singles match at Crown Jewel 2023 and in a Fatal 4-Way at Royal Rumble 2024, but he fell short both times due in large part to outside interference.

However, during Reigns' current title run, which started back at WrestleMania 42, he has gotten the job done on his own, beating challengers without help from The Bloodline.

If that holds up, then Reigns vs. Knight at Money in the Bank will mark the first fair, straight-up match between them with a world title hanging in the balance.

The fans are still firmly behind Knight and would undoubtedly love to see him accomplish his ultimate goal, but it is fair to wonder if WWE would really take the title off Reigns before WrestleMania 43.

Of course, the looming threat of 946 exists, and if they get involved, perhaps it could tip the scales in Knight's favor.

articles.title: Joey Essex wants to use younger brother Deji as his ticket to secure a KSI showdown
articles.summary: Joey Essex is hoping to secure a fight against KSI by first knocking out his younger brother, Deji.
articles.body: Joey Essex is hoping to secure a fight against KSI by first knocking out his younger brother, Deji. The reality TV star believes a victory over the YouTuber could help him earn a major crossover boxing match. Essex is preparing to face comedian Dapper Laughs at the Copper Box Arena in London on October 10.KSI, whose real name is Olajide Olayinka Williams, has not fought since losing to Tommy Fury in October 2023. Essex believes a potential victory over Deji could encourage the Misfits Boxing co-founder to return to the ring. However, the proposed fight remains an ambition rather than a confirmed contest.Joey Essex wants to fight KSI after facing DejiJoey Essex is confident that he can make a name for himself in crossover boxing. The 36-year-old wants to face Deji before pursuing a potential fight against KSI. He believes knocking out the younger Olatunji brother would strengthen his case for a showdown with the YouTube star.Speaking about his ambitions, Essex told SunSport, “Everyone wants to fight Joey Essex. That’s what I’m starting to feel like. If I was to go out there and KO KSI’s little brother, then there’s no reason why I shouldn’t be fighting KSI.”“Maybe that’s when he’ll step back in the ring. My aim is to fight the very best. Because they’re the exciting fights. Everyone wants to see that. Imagine, Joey Essex vs Jake Paul. Joey Essex vs KSI. Joey Essex vs Tommy Fury. Joey Essex vs Deji. It’s brilliant. I think they’re the fights people are going to want to see. And they’re the fights I want to do”, he said.Essex made his boxing debut in August 2025. He defeated Portuguese influencer Numeiro in his first professional crossover boxing contest. The victory gave him a positive start as he looked to establish himself in the sport.The reality TV personality has since signed a lucrative four-fight deal with Misfits Boxing. He hopes to compete approximately once every six months. His long-term ambition is to become one of the leading names in celebrity boxing.Essex also believes his popularity could help him compete with established crossover fighters. However, he recognises that several of his potential opponents have more experience inside the ring.He said, “Some of these top crossover boxers, my name is bigger than them. They’ve just had more experience in boxing than me and just been in the game a bit longer. But once I’ve been in this game for a couple of years, who’s going to be the king?”KSI remains one of the biggest names in crossover boxing. He co-founded Misfits Boxing and has competed in seven boxing bouts. His professional record includes a defeat to Tommy Fury, which came after their controversial October 2023 contest.Meanwhile, Deji has also built a following through his boxing career. articles.title: Sidney Crosby spent decades at the centre of NHL history: Inside the private family life behind the Pittsburgh Penguins icon, from his parents to his sister and upbringing in Nova Scotia
articles.summary: Delve into the private family life of Sidney Crosby, the Pittsburgh Penguins captain, and discover how his upbringing in Nova Scotia and family support shaped his iconic NHL career.
articles.body: Sidney Crosby has had a phenomenal NHL career that has made him one of the most recognisable figures in hockey, but the story off the ice has been much more private. Crosby is a gifted young player who grew up in Cole Harbour, Nova Scotia, in a close-knit family that was influential in shaping his approach to hockey and life before he became the captain of the Pittsburgh Penguins.His parents, Troy and Trina Crosby, played a big part in his early years, and his younger sister, Taylor Crosby, grew her own affinity for the game. The family as a whole provided a grounding influence as Sidney moved from a highly regarded local prospect to an NHL superstar.Sidney Crosby’s family shaped his remarkable NHL journeySidney Crosby was born on August 7, 1987, in Cole Harbour, Nova Scotia, a community just outside of Halifax that remains synonymous with his identity. His early years were spent in a relatively modest family, a far cry from the attention that would eventually surround his hockey career. The Pittsburgh Penguins have referred to the Crosby household as one of hard work, humility and strong ties to the local community.That environment became especially important as Crosby’s hockey ability began to outpace other players his age. He was skating from a young age and started in organised hockey as a kid. By the time he was a mere teenager, his playing was being noticed far beyond the borders of Nova Scotia. According to NHL.com, his father, Troy, put him on skates before he was three years old and helped teach him the fundamentals of the game.Sidney Crosby’s early hockey development began at homeIn those early years, Troy Crosby was more than just Sidney’s father; he was an important hockey influence as well. Troy, a former goalie, was drafted by the Montreal Canadiens in the 12th round of the 1984 NHL Draft. Although he never played in the NHL, he knew the game well enough from his playing days to help guide his son's development.Sidney was making remarkable rapid progress. He would play with older kids, and he always had skills that were far beyond his age group. At seven, he was already at a hockey school in Halifax for the best young players from the Maritimes. Eventually, his development took him away from home for opportunities to accelerate his path toward professional hockey.Troy Crosby and Trina Crosby supported SidneyTroy Crosby’s influence in Sidney’s development as a hockey player is well documented, but Trina Crosby’s role in the family environment that surrounded the future NHL captain was equally important. The couple raised Sidney and Taylor in Cole Harbour, focusing on the values that would keep their children grounded as their sporting ambitions grew.A stable family environment was particularly valuable for Sidney in the face of growing attention. His rise through junior hockey was met with huge expectations, and his arrival with the Pittsburgh Penguins only put him under an even bigger spotlight. But the family was also a link to the life he had lived before the fame of the professional world.Troy and Trina have also been there for important moments along their son’s career. Crosby netted his 600th NHL goal in November of 2024, and both parents were on hand at PPG Paints Arena to witness the milestone in person. Later, Crosby said it meant so much to have his family there for such a big accomplishment.Privacy has become one of the defining characteristics of Crosby's public persona. His professional achievements have been well documented, but details of his personal life have been comparatively scant.Taylor Crosby shares the family’s hockey connectionSidney’s little sister Taylor Crosby carved her own path in hockey. Taylor, eight years younger than her brother, eventually became a goaltender who played through competitive hockey programs, providing another strong bond between the Crosby family and the game.Taylor didn’t take up hockey at an extremely young age as Sidney did. She began around 10 o’clock, when Sidney was already out of town, chasing his junior career, Hockey Canada reported. Then she went to Shattuck-St. Mary’s, the same Minnesota prep school her brother played at before.Growing up with Sidney Crosby as her brother meant living with one of the sport’s biggest names, but Taylor’s own hockey journey unfolded on its own. She played at the prep level and then went on to further her education and hockey career at the collegiate level.Her relationship with Sidney, too, was distinctly a sibling affair. While they were home together and she was getting ready to go to school, Sidney kept shooting pucks at Taylor, Hockey Canada said. Taylor joked that as she improved, she was starting to block more of his shots.Sidney's job has taken him all over North America and the world, but the family has remained connected to Cole Harbour. His parents still live in the family home linked to his childhood that remains in the city, the Penguins have said.That hometown connection has translated to Crosby’s charitable work, as well. He has helped youth sports and charitable causes in Nova Scotia through his Sidney Crosby Foundation, including assisting kids looking for opportunities to get involved in sports. He has also been linked to a hockey school in Cole Harbour that has welcomed young players from other parts of the world.The result is a family saga that is not your typical celebrity story. Crosby’s career has delivered championships, international success and historic milestones, but those closest to him have generally stayed out of the constant glare of professional sports.From the influence of Troy and Trina when he was growing up to Taylor’s own hockey journey, Crosby’s family has kept him connected to the life he had before the NHL spotlight. articles.title: Fátima Gálvez suma otro oro europeo a un palmarés de leyenda
articles.standfirst: La cordobesa, campeona olímpica en Tokio 2020, se impone en la cita que se celebra en Malakasa (Grecia) tras entrar por los pelos en la final
articles.summary: La cordobesa, campeona olímpica en Tokio 2020, se impone en la cita celebrada en
articles.body: La cordobesa Fátima Gálvez, campeona olímpica en Tokio 2020 en la prueba mixta de trap, logró este viernes su tercer título europeo en foso individual durante los Campeonatos que se están disputando en Malakasa (Grecia). La tiradora de Baena, que ya se había colgado el oro en esta prueba en Belgrado 2011 y Lonato 2024, así como en mixto en Lonato 2019, no lo tuvo nada fácil para meterse entre las ocho finalistas. Necesitó un pleno de 25 en la última tanda de la clasificación y luego salió airosa del desempate (shoot-off). Posteriormente, cuajó una magnífica final. Pese a errar en el segundo tiro, enlazó diez aciertos seguidos para asegurarse una de las cuatro primeras plazas ante la eliminación, sucesivamente, de la finlandesa Sara Silja Patricia Nummela, la eslovena Jasmina Macek, la rusa Daria Semianova y la italiana Erica Sessa. Tres fallos más en las dos siguientes tandas no impidieron a Gálvez progresar. Atrás quedaron la turca Rumeysa Pelin y la italiana Jessica Rossi, y se jugó el título ante otra clásica como la italiana Silvana Maria Stanco, plata olímpica en París 2024. No falló en la última tanda la española, mientras que la italiana falló en tres platos, con lo que se hizo con la victoria con 26, dos más que su rival, en tanto que el bronce, con 20, fue para Rossi. A este oro individual hay que sumar la plata por equipos junto a Beatriz Martínez y Marc Molné, que acabaron en la vigésima y vigésima primera plaza individual, con 114 y 113 aciertos, respectivamente, a cuatro y cinco de los 118 que necesitó Gálvez para poder disputar el desempate. Con estas dos nuevas medallas, la 'tiraora' cordobesa de 39 años suma ya 15 metales continentales y siete mundiales, incluido su oro mundial individual en Lonato 2015, amén del título olímpico junto a Alberto Fernández en la capital japonesa. Su primera gran medalla, en foso por equipos, fue el bronce europeo de Kazán 2010 por lo que Fátima lleva ya 17 años en la élite de su disciplina. Además tiene tres diplomas olímpicos individuales merced a su cuarto puesto en Río 2016 y los dos quintos de Londres 2012 y París 2024. Sin duda, un historial de leyenda.
