articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 5 Fades & Busts: Jalen Hurts is officially out of the top 12
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Matt Okada fades some startable players in Week 5.
articles.body:
Welcome to the fifth of 17 weekly articles spotlighting the fantasy fades of the week! I am your host, Matt Okada, and I'll be bringing you half a dozen potential busts each and every Friday, from now until fantasy championships.

As a note, just because a player earns a "fade" or "bust" designation doesn't automatically mean they should be benched — it depends on the rest of your roster or the options on your waiver wire. But you can expect them to fall short of expectations (when I get them right). I include a "What to Do" section for every player to help with that.

Without further ado, here is my list for Week 5 of the 2026 season.

Jalen Hurts' name and Jalen Hurts' recent production simply do not occupy the same tier anymore. He's scored progressively fewer fantasy points each week this season, from 24.72 in Week 1 down to 13.62 and 13.52, respectively, the last two weeks.

A variety of reasons, but probably the biggest one is the decline in his rushing production. From 2021 through 2024, Jalen Hurts averaged 9.5 fantasy points per game as a rusher, comfortably the most by any quarterback. But since the start of last season, that average has dropped by 44%, as Hurts has rushed for just 26 yards per game over that span and has scored just once on the ground over his last nine starts . And unfortunately, he's not compensating as a passer in 2026, with just 178.3 passing yards per game.

After dicing up the Commanders in Week 1 — which doesn't carry all that much weight given how their defense has played — Hurts has thrown four touchdowns and three interceptions in the three games since. Now he enters a matchup with the Jaguars, who held Drake Maye, Bo Nix and Deshaun Watson outside the top-18 fantasy quarterbacks in each of their respective matchups. The Jags have allowed just three touchdown passes and snagged six interceptions through the first month, the best TD-INT ratio by any defense so far. While Hurts might still feel like a top-end QB1, the data does not support that feeling this season or this week.

What to do ❓ As crazy as it might seem, Hurts is outside the top-12 quarterbacks for Week 5 and can absolutely be benched for streamers like Jacoby Brissett, Jameis Winston, C.J. Stroud and others.

Speaking of players whose elite fantasy history and current fantasy output don't match up ... David Montgomery has been awful. He unfortunately fooled fantasy managers with a 28.9-point, three-touchdown performance in Week 1, but has since been a major disappointment. Over the last three contests, he's averaged just 4.5 fantasy points and 22.3 rushing yards per game. He hasn't had more than 60 rushing yards in a game all year (even including Week 1). Since Week 2, he sports the position's second-fewest yards per carry (2.7), lowest success rate (23.4%) and lowest explosive run rate (2.1%). He's losing snaps and drives to Woody Marks and appears to be entirely touchdown-dependent for fantasy.

If Houston doesn't find its way into the red zone several times in a game, there appears to be absolutely no ceiling (or floor, frankly) for Montgomery. The Titans aren't exactly a standout matchup one way or another, though they've allowed the seventh-fewest yards per carry to running backs, so this is more of a PSA for fantasy managers still riding the high of opening weekend. Montgomery is borderline unplayable right now, and we need to adjust accordingly.

What to do ❓ I know running back looks incredibly shallow right now, but the fact that Montgomery is still outside RB2 range in that context should tell you everything you need to know. You're better off starting a replacement back like Braelon Allen or Emanuel Wilson, or a committee back like Kyle Monangai (or RJ Harvey in any form of PPR).

Jacory Croskey-Merritt, RB, Commanders vs. Giants

Jacory Croskey-Merritt is sort of a lesser version of Montgomery. He had a decent Week 1 — 63 rushing yards and a touchdown — but has averaged just 5.4 fantasy points per game since, with fewer than 45 rushing yards in all contests and zero touchdowns since Week 1. He's also been horribly inefficient, ranking bottom 10 among qualified running backs in success rate, EPA per carry, missed tackle rate and explosive run rate. Possibly as a result or due to Rachaad White's injury, the Commanders signed Austin Ekeler before Week 4. It's bad news for JCM either way.

The veteran immediately outproduced Croskey-Merritt in the ground game — on far fewer carries and snaps — and seems like a major threat to the younger back's role and upside in the offense. As with the Titans against Montgomery, the Giants aren't a difficult matchup, but it doesn't particularly matter in this case. Neither the volume nor the efficiency for Croskey-Merritt offers any confidence in his floor or ceiling.

What to do ❓ Unfortunately for those who drafted "Bill" in the middle rounds hoping for a value RB2, he simply cannot be played except in the most dire of circumstances. Consider him a low-end FLEX at best.

Courtland Sutton, WR, Broncos at Chargers

I'll admit off the rip, Courtland Sutton has been so ineffective for fantasy that this "Fade" should be unnecessary, and some of you will probably question his inclusion at all. However, with Sutton still rostered in 70% of Yahoo leagues and Pat Bryant likely to miss Sunday's game against the Chargers, there will be a surprising number of fantasy managers tempted to slot Sutton into their lineup for one last shot at redemption.

Through four games, Sutton has already had a 17.6% target share, second on the team to Jaylen Waddle's 20.8%, well ahead of Bryant's 9.6%. Bryant has stood out for fantasy because he's averaged 11.1 yards per target, with a 75.0% catch rate and a touchdown, but he's only seen 12 targets in total. Meanwhile, Sutton has been abysmal with his volume, averaging 3.9 yards per target with a 40.9% catch rate, both the worst marks by any player with 20+ targets in the entire league. Even if you gifted Bryant's three targets per game entirely to Sutton, at his rate of 0.6 half-PPR fantasy points per target, that would equate to a boost of just 1.8 fantasy points. As with the running backs above, the Chargers are actually a soft matchup for wide receivers, but it just doesn't matter with the way Sutton is playing this season. Frankly, if he doesn't prove me wrong with a vintage game this week, he's probably going to be droppable come the Week 6 waiver run.

What to do ❓ Do not start Sutton under basically any circumstance. Even in deeper leagues or on rosters with extra WR slots, I'd rather play guys like Kalif Raymond, Wan'Dale Robinson, Tre' Harris in the same game or even waiver wire adds Keon Coleman and Dohnte Meyers.

Disclaimer: I believe in Josh Downs as a talent. He's an excellent route-runner and a separation specialist, and in an offense with a capable, accurate quarterback and a smart, high-volume offensive scheme, he might be a fantasy WR1. Unfortunately, as we saw in London last Sunday, the Colts' passing game is a mess. Daniel Jones has the league's sixth-lowest passer rating and third-lowest EPA per dropback (ahead of only Baker Mayfield and Jameis Winston) and has been pressured 60 times through four games, sixth-most for any quarterback. He's thrown for fewer than 170 yards twice and does not have multiple touchdown passes in a single game this season ... but does have an interception in every game.

In ideal circumstances with Keenan Allen inactive (and Alec Pierce still on IR) against the Commanders defense, Downs had just three catches on four targets for 16 yards last Sunday. The leading receiver on the team was Laquon Treadwell, with just 42 yards, and Jones finished with just 143 passing yards and no TDs against a team that had previously allowed 291.7 yards per game and 11 touchdowns in three games . Allen is likely to return this week and the Steelers' pass defense has been far more effective than Washington's. Until proven otherwise, there's simply no ceiling for Downs in this offense and the floor is fewer than five fantasy points (which has happened twice).

What to do ❓ Considering how good he looked in Weeks 2 and 3, Downs isn't a must-sit like Sutton, as he could have another okay day purely on volume — think six catches for 70 yards and exactly 10 fantasy points. But if that's as good as you're going to get, there are a number of better WR3 or FLEX plays.

Joe Brady and the Bills have some explaining to do with regard to Dalton Kincaid, and we actually saw him try after the Patriots game. What do I mean? Well, over the first two weeks, Kincaid had a 25% target share and 30% air yards share in Buffalo and was averaging a position-high 4.7 yards per route run. He looked legitimately elite and was featured in my Week 2 Stock Report here at Yahoo. In the two weeks since? Kincaid's dropped to a 9% target share, 11% air yards share and just 1.2 yards per route run.

This has always seemed to happen with Kincaid over the years in Buffalo — his production is excellent, even elite, but his usage and offensive role never seem to consistently reflect that. And unfortunately, it's hard to see him bouncing back in a matchup with the Rams. Los Angeles has allowed a league-low 85 receiving yards to tight ends through one month.

Not 85 yards per game ... 85 yards total .

They're No. 1 against the position in yards per target (2.9) and have not allowed a single explosive catch to tight ends all year. For fantasy, they're allowing just 5.13 points per game to the position and held both Isaiah Likely and George Kittle (albeit in Week 1) to fewer than eight fantasy points. I really like Kincaid as a fantasy asset and sincerely hope Brady and Co. utilize him correctly rest-of-season ... but I'm fading him for one more week with this defense on the docket.

What to do ❓ Tight end is a shallow position, and Kincaid really is that good, so even with everything I've said above, he's a fringe TE1. But he's certainly not the top-five play he was after the first couple of weeks, and you should absolutely play Likely, Colston Loveland, Juwan Johnson and Tucker Kraft over him and could consider streamers like Mike Gesicki and T.J. Hockenson as well.

articles.title: Man City case causing ‘uncertainty’ for whole Premier League, says Iraola
articles.summary: Liverpool’s Andoni Iraola looks to Manchester City clash and rival’s appeal over guilty verdict for financial breaches.
articles.body:
Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola said the lack of clarity over Manchester City’s future after the club was found guilty of multiple breaches of financial rules was causing uncertainty throughout the Premier League.

City remain adamant they have done no wrong and have appealed against the findings of an independent commission announced last week.

The Premier League leaders potentially face a severe points deduction that threatens their place in the English top flight.

Iraola believes the world’s richest league is caught in limbo until there is a definitive outcome.

“I think the worst thing probably is the uncertainty, that no one knows what’s going to happen,” the Spaniard said ahead of City’s first outing since the verdict at Liverpool on Sunday.

“But we have to focus on Liverpool – be the best club we can be, the best team we can be and that’s my challenge.”

Iraola only joined the Reds in June but is looking forward to a red-hot atmosphere at home.

“The atmosphere is going to be big, especially at Anfield,” he said.

“We want to give also our supporters reasons to be with us. When they see the team they want to see on the pitch, we can create an even better atmosphere and we will work for that.”

Liverpool are still unbeaten under Iraola, but three draws in their opening five league games means they start the weekend six points off the top.

Iraola’s options up front are limited after Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo were injured on international duty.

“As a club manager, you are always waiting until the game ends (hoping) the doctor doesn’t call you, doesn’t give you bad news, but in this case we’ve been unlucky with Alex and Cody, both of them,” he said.

“They are injured and they are not going to be involved on Sunday.”

articles.title: Graeme Dott: Ex-world snooker champion intends to appeal against conviction and jail sentence for child sex abuse
articles.summary: Warning: This article contains details of child sexual abuse; Graeme Dott was last month jailed for seven years for preying on two primary school-age children. A young girl was targeted between 1993 and 1996, and a boy from 2006 to 2010
articles.body:
Warning: This article contains details of child sexual abuse.

Dott was jailed last month and was told his name would be placed on the sex offenders' register indefinitely.

The shamed sportsman, 49, denied any wrongdoing but was in August found guilty of lewd, indecent and libidinous practices and behaviour towards two primary school-aged children.

The allegations spanned between 1993 and 1996 involving a girl in Glasgow, and 2006 to 2010 involving a boy in South Lanarkshire.

Judge Lord Harrower said Dott robbed his victims of "a significant part of their childhood", adding: "Your behaviour towards them bore the classic hallmarks of grooming."

On Friday, the Scottish Courts and Tribunals Service (SCTS) confirmed to Sky News an intimation of intention to appeal against his conviction and sentence had been lodged.

The note of appeal is due by December 3.

During Dott's trial at the High Court in Glasgow, jurors heard how he repeatedly molested his two victims.

This included inducing the girl to briefly engage in a sex act, which came to an end when she "started to cry", and sexually abusing the boy while the youngster was in a shower.

Both victims, now adults, told the court they received gifts from Dott at the time of his abuse.

The woman said she was once given a teddy, which had a love heart on it that read "love me".

The man said he was gifted snacks and treats - including a £50 note - as a "reward strategy".

Dott refuted the pair's claims, branding the allegations "disgusting".

During Dott's sentencing, defence lawyer Euan Dow said his client continued to maintain his innocence and had the support of his family and friends.

Mr Dow said Dott had "received threats" in jail and had been moved to another section as a result of becoming "a target within the custodial establishment".

Dott turned professional in 1994 and went on to win the World Snooker Championship in 2006, defeating Peter Ebdon in the final at the Crucible in Sheffield.

He also reached the final in both 2004, when he was beaten by Ronnie O'Sullivan, and 2010, losing to Australian Neil Robertson.

Dott was suspended from competition by the World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association (WPBSA) when the court charges were announced in April 2025.

Following his conviction, his membership was "permanently revoked" and he was additionally removed from World Snooker Tour's hall of fame.

Procurator Fiscal Faye Cook, of the Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service (COPFS), said at the time of his sentencing: "Graeme Dott achieved success and public admiration but, in private, he exploited the trust of two children to abuse and coerce them.

"Dott's criminal behaviour has been his downfall, and he now faces the consequences of his actions."
authors: Jenness Mitchell, Sky News Scotland reporter

articles.title: Shakira y Serge Ibaka: el nuevo rumor de un romance que nace de un avión privado
articles.standfirst: Vinculan a Shakira con el exjugador de la NBA Serge Ibaka: lo que se sabe de su cercano encuentro
articles.summary: Vinculan a Shakira con el exjugador de la NBA Serge Ibaka: lo que se sabe de su cercano encuentro
articles.body: Los rumores sobre la vida sentimental de Shakira han tomado un nuevo rumbo en España. Según reportes difundidos por periodistas del entretenimiento en Europa y Estados Unidos, la artista colombiana estaría compartiendo momentos cercanos con Serge Ibaka, exjugador profesional de la NBA y figura destacada del baloncesto internacional. Las versiones sobre este posible vínculo cobraron fuerza a través de declaraciones del periodista Jordi Martín, corresponsal en España del programa El Gordo y la Flaca (Univision). De acuerdo con el comunicador, el deportista de 37 años habría asistido a varios de los conciertos de la cantante en Madrid y, posteriormente, ambos habrían compartido trayectos en un avión privado. Las sospechas entre sus seguidores comenzaron a finales de septiembre, cuando asistentes a sus presentaciones compartieron videos de la barranquillera interpretando el tema Antología, relacionando la emotividad de la presentación con la presencia del baloncestista entre el público. El rumor tomó mayor tracción en medios de prensa rosa como Las Mamarazzis y programas conducidos por periodistas de la televisión española. Serge Jonás Ibaka Ngobila es una figura reconocida tanto dentro como fuera de las canchas de baloncesto. Nació en Brazzaville (República del Congo) en 1989. Enfrentó una infancia compleja tras perder a su madre a los ocho años y vivir el encarcelamiento de su padre. Llegó a España a los 17 años para desarrollarse profesionalmente en el CB L'Hospitalet y el Ricoh Manresa. Fue seleccionado en la primera ronda del Draft de 2008 y jugó 14 temporadas en la liga estadounidense con franquicias como Oklahoma City Thunder, Orlando Magic, Toronto Raptors (equipo con el que se coronó campeón en 2019), Los Angeles Clippers y Milwaukee Bucks. Tras obtener la nacionalidad española en 2011, conquistó la medalla de oro en el Eurobasket 2011 y la medalla de plata en los Juegos Olímpicos de Londres 2012 con la selección de España. Fuera del deporte, Ibaka ha explorado la industria musical con proyectos Afrobeat. Su sencillo Champion (junto al rapero Ninho) superó los 35 millones de reproducciones en plataformas digitales. Estos rumores surgen durante la estancia de Shakira en la capital española, donde realiza una serie de presentaciones multitudinarias en el marco de su residencia musical, cuya fecha de cierre está programada para el 12 de octubre en el Estadio Shakira con capacidad para 50.000 personas. Hasta el momento, ni la cantante ni el deportista han emitido declaraciones oficiales para confirmar o desmentir las versiones sobre su cercanía.

articles.title: Falleció Eduardo Vilarete: se conoce la última voluntad del exfutbolista colombiano para su familia
articles.standfirst: Revelan la emotiva última voluntad de Eduardo Vilarete: el especial pedido que le hizo a su familia antes de morir
articles.summary: Revelan la emotiva última voluntad de Eduardo Vilarete: el especial pedido que le hizo a su familia antes de morir
articles.body: El fútbol colombiano se viste de luto tras confirmarse el sensible fallecimiento de Eduardo Emilio Vilarete Fernández a sus 73 años de edad en la ciudad de Bogotá. Reconocido por su potencia física, temperamento en la cancha y un olfato goleador implacable que superó los 200 tantos en su carrera profesional, Vilarete dejó una huella imborrable en clubes icónicos como Atlético Nacional, Unión Magdalena, Deportes Tolima, Atlético Bucaramanga y Deportivo Pereira, además de defender la camiseta de la Selección Colombia. En las últimas horas, a través de un comunicado oficial, la familia del exdelantero dio a conocer los detalles sobre sus exequias y reveló cuál fue la última voluntad que pidió expresamente antes de su deceso. Cumpliendo con el deseo expreso de Eduardo Vilarete antes de su partida, sus funerales y exequias principales se llevarán a cabo en la ciudad de Ibagué (Tolima), territorio donde el exfutbolista dejó gratos recuerdos en su paso por el Deportes Tolima y donde construyó un fuerte lazo afectivo en su vida personal y familiar. Posteriormente, la familia confirmó que sus restos o cenizas serán trasladados a Santa Marta, su ciudad natal, donde se le rendirá un sentido homenaje de despedida en la tierra donde dio sus primeros pasos como deportista y donde es considerado una leyenda inmortal del Unión Magdalena. "Cumpliendo con su última voluntad, sus exequias se realizarán en la ciudad de Ibagué y posteriormente se le rendirá un homenaje en su natal Santa Marta, compartiendo oportunamente los detalles con quienes deseen acompañarnos", expresó la familia en el comunicado oficial. Durante los últimos meses, el 'Loco' Vilarete venía atravesando un delicado estado de salud debido a un diagnóstico de sarcoma (un tipo de cáncer) detectado en su pierna izquierda. El avance de la enfermedad obligó a una junta médica a recomendar la amputación de su extremidad como alternativa para intentar salvar su vida; decisión que el propio exfutbolista aceptó con entereza en agosto de 2026. A pesar del esfuerzo médico y el acompañamiento constante de sus seres queridos, diversas complicaciones derivadas de su enfermedad desencadenaron su deceso en la capital del país. Nacido en Santa Marta en 1953, Eduardo Emilio Vilarete fue una de las referencias ofensivas más temidas del fútbol sudamericano entre la década de 1970 y mediados de los 80. La Dimayor, la Federación Colombiana de Fútbol y los diferentes clubes donde militó han expresado sus condolencias a familiares y allegados, destacando a Vilarete no solo como un futbolista extraordinario dentro de la cancha, sino como un referente de carisma y entrega que marcó a toda una generación del deporte nacional.

articles.title: El deporte español pide recuperar el IVA reducido del 10%
articles.standfirst: La Asociación del Deporte Español y la Federación Española de Golf presentan una propuesta para volver al tipo del 10% para los servicios deportivos en vez del 21% en vigor desde 2012
articles.summary: La Asociación del Deporte Español y la Federación Española de Golf presentan una propuesta para volver al tipo del 10% para los servicios deportivos en vez del 21% en vigor desde 2012
articles.body: La Asociación del Deporte Español (ADESP), la entidad que agrupa a las federaciones nacionales deportivas, y la Real Federación Española de Golf (RFEG) presentaron una propuesta a favor de que los servicios vinculados a la práctica deportiva en España vuelva a tener un IVA reducido del diez por ciento en vez del 21 por ciento actual. La iniciativa se dio a conocer en una rueda de prensa en el Real Club de Campo Villa de Madrid, donde se celebra el Open de España de golf. El IVA de los servicios deportivos pasó del 8 al 21 por ciento en septiembre de 2012 debido a la crisis económica con el fin de generar más ingresos. En el acto se dio a conocer un informe según el cual la rebaja del IVA no reduciría la recaudación final porque la bajada inicial de ingresos se compensaría con creces con el aumento de la demanda y del turismo, la generación de empleo y la reducción de los costes sanitarios, entre otros efectos positivos. "Tenemos que reivindicar lo que somos. La cultura sí ha conseguido un IVA reducido. ¿Por qué un cheque cultural y no uno deportivo?", se preguntó José Hidalgo, presidente de ADESP. Hidalgo anunció que en los próximos días se va a reunir con representantes de los partidos políticos para trasladarles la propuesta y otras demandas del sector, como una ley de patrocinio del deporte similar a la de mecenazgo para la cultura. Además de Hidalgo, intervinieron en la rueda de prensa el presidente de la RFEG, Juan Guerrero-Burgos; el de la Asociación Española de Campos de Golf, Luis Nigorra, y el autor del informe, Alberto García Varela, de EY Abogados. "No pedimos una excepción para el golf. Usamos los datos del golf para demostrar lo que una fiscalidad favorable a la práctica deportiva puede hacer por toda la economía", argumentó Nigorra. Los promotores de la iniciativa alegaron que buena parte de los países europeos tiene un IVA reducido para la práctica deportiva, como Suecia y Bélgica (6 %), Irlanda (9 %) o Países Bajos (10 %).

articles.title: Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero siguen arrasando y vuelven a amenazar a las número uno
articles.standfirst: La pareja catalana certifica su gran estado de forma tras dos títulos consecutivos y se medirá en semifinales del Germany P2 a Gemma Triay y Delfi Brea
articles.summary: La pareja catalana certifica su gran estado de forma tras dos títulos consecutivos y se medirá en semifinales del Germany P2 a Gemma Triay y Delfi Brea
articles.body: Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero continúan consolidándose como la dupla más en forma del circuito femenino. Tras superar un tramo de temporada marcado por la irregularidad en sus resultados, la reusense y la barcelonesa han encadenado una dinámica de juego que les ha permitido conquistar los dos últimos torneos disputados y recortar distancias en la clasificación general. En la penúltima ronda del Germany P2 en Düsseldorf, Sánchez y Ustero se medirán a las número uno del ranking FIP, Gemma Triay y Delfi Brea. Ambas parejas volverán a verse las caras tras el precedente de las semifinales de Rotterdam, en un duelo directo con implicaciones clave para la lucha por la zona alta de la tabla en el tramo final del curso. La dupla dirigida por Ángel González certificó su pase a semifinales tras resolver su cruce de cuartos de final frente a Alejandra Salazar y Aranza Osoro. Pese a que las condiciones de la pista indoor alemana favorecían el estilo de juego de sus rivales, Sánchez y Ustero dominaron el encuentro de principio a fin, imponiendo un ritmo elevado que se tradujo en un doble 6-1 en menos de una hora de partido. Por su parte, Triay y Brea aseguraron su clasificación tras superar a Claudia Jensen y Noa Cánovas por 6-3 y 6-1. La menorquina y la argentina venían de completar un exigente compromiso de octavos de final ante Marta Barrera y Jana Montes, logrando elevar su rendimiento en cuartos para volver a acercarse a la pelea por títulos. En el otro lado del cuadro femenino, las semifinales de Düsseldorf acogerán un nuevo enfrentamiento entre Paula Josemaría y Bea González frente a Claudia Fernández y Martina Calvo, reeditando el choque de la pasada semana en tierras neerlandesas. Josemaría y González accedieron a la penúltima ronda tras imponerse con autoridad a Marina Guinart y Alejandra Alonso. La extremeña y la malagueña controlaron el ritmo de los intercambios de principio a fin, cerrando el choque con un contundente 6-0 y 6-1. Asimismo, Fernández y Calvo sellaron su presencia entre las cuatro mejores parejas del torneo al vencer a Marta Ortega y Sofía Araújo. La dupla hispano-navarra mostró solvencia en las áreas de definición para adjudicarse la victoria por 6-0 y 6-3, garantizando su presencia en la jornada de sábado por sexto torneo consecutivo.

articles.title: El contundente mensaje de Nayib Bukele para el 'Bolillo' Gómez
articles.standfirst: El Estado da su respaldo al técnico tras la crisis de la Selección de El Salvador
articles.summary: El Estado da su respaldo al técnico tras la crisis de la Selección de El Salvador
articles.body: El futuro de Hernán Darío 'Bolillo' Gómez al frente de la selección mayor de El Salvador sigue concentrando la atención del fútbol latinoamericano. A pesar de los momentos de tensión y los resultados adversos en la Liga de Naciones de la Concacaf, la postura oficial en El Salvador ha enviado un mensaje de compromiso total y respaldo al estratega colombiano para consolidar un proyecto deportivo a largo plazo. El mandatario de El Salvador, Nayib Bukele, dejó en claro la disposición de su administración para brindar todas las garantías y recursos necesarios para el desarrollo del fútbol nacional, abordándolo no solo como una disciplina deportiva, sino como un proyecto de país. "Lo que podamos hacer nosotros lo vamos a hacer. No hay ninguna cosa que no podamos dar, ni que no vayamos a poner. Esto no se va a parar por recursos, ni por logística, ni por leyes, ni por nacionalizaciones, ni por burocracia, por nada. Vamos a dar todo lo que sea necesario. Todo el país lo vamos a movilizar para lograrlo", enfatizó el presidente salvadoreño. Por su parte, el 'Bolillo' Gómez destacó el valor transformador del deporte como un elemento capaz de unificar e inspirar a la sociedad salvadoreña: "Una selección puede unir a un país. El país nos va a sacar adelante porque ya hay optimismo, y démosle una alegría al país. Este acercamiento me da seguridad", declaró el técnico colombiano tras reunirse con las autoridades locales. Paralelamente, la Federación Salvadoreña de Fútbol (Fesfut), encabezada por Yamil Bukele, confirmó la continuidad de Gómez al frente de 'La Selecta', señalando que cortar el proceso supondría un retroceso de casi un año de trabajo. Sin embargo, la dirigencia aclaró que la confianza brindada exige una alta cuota de responsabilidad y que la permanencia del estratega no constituye un "cheque en blanco". Con el respaldo institucional garantizado y la mirada puesta en las siguientes fases competitivas de la Concacaf, 'Bolillo' Gómez afronta el reto de reestructurar el rendimiento del equipo nacional en busca de los resultados exigidos por la afición.

articles.title: Todo a punto para el estreno del Hyatlón Ambar Tour en Madrid
articles.standfirst: Casi 1.000 deportistas competirán este fin de semana en la capital madrileña en Gallur
articles.summary: Casi 1.000 deportistas competirán este fin de semana en la capital madrileña en Gallur
articles.body: La Federación Española de Triatlón (FETRI) ha presentado este viernes en el Centro Deportivo Municipal (CDM) Gallur de Madrid el Hyatlón Ambar Tour, su nuevo circuito de fitness racing, que combina carrera a pie y estaciones funcionales. El acto se celebró en la misma instalación que acoge este fin de semana la primera prueba del calendario. Asistieron al acto representantes de la Comunidad de Madrid, del Ayuntamiento de Madrid y de la Federación Madrileña de Triatlón, junto a las empresas que respaldan el proyecto desde su origen. El presidente de la FETRI, José Hidalgo, subrayó el carácter pionero de un circuito que, según explicó, se pone en marcha por primera vez a nivel mundial y que ya despierta interés fuera de España: “Hacía falta visión y valentía para involucrarse en un proyecto que arranca sin ningún libro donde mirar”, señaló Hidalgo, que agradeció a los patrocinadores su confianza en una iniciativa que, en sus palabras, “no era más que un papel y mucho entusiasmo”. Hidalgo planteó estas cuatro primeras competiciones como parte de una curva de aprendizaje, en la que la Federación escuchará el feedback de los deportistas. También defendió el papel de la FETRI en la federalización de la modalidad, que aporta seguridad jurídica, legitimidad y un recorrido que, de la mano de la Federación Internacional, puede llegar a ser olímpico. El circuito buscará además generar valor para el deportista antes, durante y después de la competición, con especial peso de la integración tecnológica. La primera cita llega con las inscripciones cerradas desde hace una semana. La organización se había marcado un objetivo de entre 800 y 1.000 deportistas y la cifra final se sitúa en 998 participantes, un límite fijado para garantizar el control de la prueba en su estreno. La competición se desarrollará el sábado de 8:00 a 19:30 horas y durante toda la jornada del domingo. Por parte de la Comunidad de Madrid, Alberto Tomé, Director General de Deportes, destacó el auge del atleta híbrido, que combina fuerza y resistencia, y el valor de dar el pistoletazo de salida en Gallur, una pista por la que han pasado algunos de los mejores atletas del mundo. Tomé, que competirá en la prueba, puso en valor la colaboración público-privada como garantía de éxito en las políticas deportivas de la región. La Concejala Delegada de Deporte del Ayuntamiento de Madrid, Sonia Cea, agradeció a la Federación que eligiera la capital para iniciar el proyecto y aseguró que esta será “la primera edición de muchas” en la ciudad. Cea destacó el alto porcentaje de participación femenina, en torno al 35%, y el carácter integrador de una modalidad exigente pero abierta a todos los públicos. Al acto asistió también Gregorio Ramírez, Director General de Deporte del Ayuntamiento de Madrid. Ambar, que da nombre al circuito, explicó a través de su Responsable de Comunicación y Patrocinios, Andrea Anguita, que fue la propia marca quien se dirigió a la Federación para sumarse al proyecto. Anguita vinculó la apuesta con las ganas de innovar de la marca y con una demanda social creciente: personas que quieren cuidarse y que prestan atención tanto a su preparación deportiva como a su alimentación. Joma, representada por su Responsable de Patrocinios, Hugo Herraiz, calificó la presentación de paso histórico. Herraiz explicó que contactó con la Federación en cuanto conoció el proyecto por la sintonía de valores entre ambas partes, y resumió la filosofía de la marca: “para evolucionar hay que apostar por nuevas ideas, con valentía y pasión.” Suzuki, socio habitual de la FETRI, estuvo representada por Juan López, Presidente de Suzuki Ibérica, que enmarcó su apoyo en la innovación y la mejora continua que forman parte del ADN de la compañía. López recordó que no hizo falta que se lo pidieran: cuando conoció el proyecto, fue él quien quiso sumarse. Matrix Fitness, a través de su CEO, Ernesto Aspe, describió su participación como una vuelta a sus orígenes. La compañía, nacida hace 50 años, ha acompañado durante décadas al deportista en su entrenamiento, pero no en la pista de competición. Con el Hyatlón, el equipamiento de fitness pasa a ser la herramienta del deportista, como lo es el balón en otras disciplinas. NooFit, representada por su CEO, Javier Núñez, destacó que el Hyatlón ofrece a los miles de deportistas que entrenan cada día en gimnasios y centros deportivos un objetivo concreto y una fecha en el calendario. La compañía aporta su tecnología para que los participantes puedan medir sus entrenamientos y comprobar su progresión. MARCA, media partner del circuito, estuvo representada por su director, Juan Ignacio Gallardo, que destacó la capacidad de estos nuevos formatos para conectar con públicos que no siempre llegan a las disciplinas tradicionales. Gallardo se mostró orgulloso de participar en el nacimiento del proyecto y de contribuir desde la comunicación a su crecimiento, con el horizonte olímpico como meta. Completa el grupo de patrocinadores 226ERS, marca española de nutrición deportiva que acompaña al circuito desde su origen. Su presencia responde a una de las claves de la modalidad: en una prueba que alterna carrera y estaciones de fuerza, la gestión de la energía es tan determinante como la preparación física. Tras el estreno en Madrid, el Hyatlón Ambar Tour continuará su recorrido por España. HYATLÓN Madrid (Formato H6): 10 y 11 de octubre en el CDM Gallur. HYATLÓN La Nucía (Formato H6): 24 y 25 de octubre en el Combat Sport Center. HYATLÓN Gran Canaria (Formato H6): 14 y 15 de noviembre en la Plaza de la Música, dentro de ExpoDeca. HYATLÓN Zaragoza (Formato H8): 28 y 29 de noviembre en el Pabellón 4 de Feria de Zaragoza.

articles.title: Jesús Fraile logra la medalla de bronce en el Grand Prix de París
articles.standfirst: El español ganó este viernes la primera presea para la delegación española
articles.summary: El español ganó este viernes la primera presea para la delegación española
articles.body: Jesús Fraile (-58 kg) ganó este viernes la medalla de bronce, la primera para la delegación española, en la jornada inaugural del Grand Prix de taekwondo de París-Levallois, tras alcanzar las semifinales de su categoría. Fraile inició su participación con una victoria por 2-0 ante el también español Jairo Agenjo en los dieciseisavos de final y luego superó por 2-1 al griego Konstantinos Dimitropoulos en octavos y al brasileño Paulo Melo en cuartos. En las semifinales, el madrileño cayó ante el iraní Abolfazl Zandi, vigente campeón mundial, por lo que quedó apeado de la lucha por el oro. En la misma jornada, Iván García consiguió un diploma tras finalizar quinto en la categoría de más de 80 kilos. El español cayó por 1-2 ante el británico Cunningham en cuartos de final. Por su parte, Sergio Troitiño, también en más de 80 kilos, perdió por 1-2 ante el ruso Larin. En categoría femenina, Tania María Castiñeira (+67 kg) cayó por 0-2 ante la uzbeka Saidova en octavos de final; y Belén Morán (+80 kg) fue eliminada en su debut por 0-2 ante la serbia Bozanic. La competición continuará este sábado con la participación de otros cuatro españoles. Adrián Vicente (-68 kg), Alma María Pérez (-57 kg), Laura Rodríguez (-57 kg) y Lena Moreno (-67 kg) entrarán en acción en la segunda jornada del campeonato. La medalla de Fraile se suma al bronce conseguido el jueves por el español Joel Martín Villalobos en la competición de parataekwondo.

articles.title: Why you should keep starting Jaguars WR in fantasy football after down week
articles.summary: Despite a quiet Week 4 performance, one fantasy football analyst believes you should continue to start this Jaguars' wide receiver.
articles.body:
Last week was relatively quiet for Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington, who caught just one pass for seven yards, while totaling just 2.0 fantasy football points.

However, if you're debating whether or not to start Washington this week, ESPN's Eric Moody is here to provide the obvious answer -- start him.

" Jaguars WR Parker Washington has scored at least 13 fantasy points in three of four games this season, so I wouldn't be too concerned about his 2.0-point Week 4 performance," Moody wrote. "He also had a 39-yard reception overturned."

While trying to project what the target share for each of the Jaguars' receivers will look like on a weekly basis in Liam Coen's offense can be a difficult task, through the second half of last season, Washington emerged as a favorite target of Trevor Lawrence.

That high volume target share has continued into this season, with Washington hauling in 16 receptions on 25 passes through four games, not to mention that he's found success generating several explosive plays through the air as well.

League-wide, Washington has been one of the more efficient pass-catching targets, ranking 17th in PFF's yards per route run metric.

"Washington is in a good spot to bounce back against a defense that has allowed the 10th-most fantasy points per game to WRs and has struggled against slot receivers," Moody added.

articles.title: WBA claims it did not approve Jaime Munguia vs Nikita Zon
articles.summary: The WBA might be experiencing a rare pang of conscience over Jaime Munguia’s ducking of Bektemir Melikuziev
articles.body:
In case you're just joining us, something weird is happening at super middleweight.

Late last month, the WBA ordered newly crowned champion Jaime Munguia (46-2, 35 KO) to face mandatory challenger Bektemir "Bek the Bully" Melikuziev (17-1, 11 KO), who's been owed a title shot since edging out Darius Fulghum in an eliminator in May of last year. Munguia, seeking a spot on the Canelo vs Mbilli undercard against a more manageable opponent, sought to pay Melikuziev some step-aside money , which Melikuziev publicly rejected.

This made it strange when Munguia appeared on yesterday's undercard announcement opposite amateur standout turned unremarkable pro Nikita Zon (12-0-1, 10 KO). The poster bizarrely listed Munguia vs Zon as a "WBA Super Middleweight Fight" in contrast to Rafael Espinoza vs Lorenzo Parra and Lindolfo Delgado vs Arthur Biyarslanov, which it clearly labeled as title bouts.

We might now know why, as the WBA announced on social media that they "ha[ve] not approved" the fight and "will review the situation."

The only real remedy here is to strip Munguia. If they give him a slap on the wrist and let the fight go through with the stipulation that Munguia has to fight Melikuziev within X number of days, it's punishing Melikuziev for not taking the payoff. Same with doing their usual title shuffle and making Munguia "champion in recess" or something.

The WBA are the most cartoonishly amoral of the sanctioning bodies, but they've retreated in the face of concentrated backlash before, and what little bits of optimism dot my blackened soul think they might actually recognize accommodating Munguia's shenanigans as a step too far. We can hope, at least.

articles.title: Notes from Big Ten MBB Media Day
articles.summary: How the faces of Big Ten basketball feel about their teams, the transfer portal and more.
articles.body:
All the best sound bites from Big Ten MBB Media Day in Rosemont. Some of these quotes have been edited for brevity and clarity.

Junior forward Angelo Ciaravino about stepping into a leadership role with the team: "Being here for two years and being under guys like Brooks and Nick and Ty and Matt, being able to learn from them has been great for me. And now, stepping into that bigger leadership role, I felt pretty comfortable showing the new guys the culture and the way we run things."

Ciaravino on his focus in the offseason: "I would say just focusing on my strengths, honestly. Just keeping that physicality, strengthening that physicality. I stepped into the bigger leadership role. So I would say that was a huge one for me: just being a better leader on the court, off the court, and bringing these guys together and just kind of shaping this team up to be where it needs to be."

Ciaravino on learning from the new faces in the locker room: "It's cool to just hear everyone's different perspective and where they came from and how they did things at their schools. You can kind of just pick everyone's brain a little bit and just find ways that we can improve what we have going on. And I feel like that's definitely a big part of all these new guys and they've been super great about sharing their experiences, sharing what went right at their schools and what went wrong and what they feel like we should have in our program and what we should be doing. So I feel like it's been super great having these guys."

Ciaravino on how the team will replace Nick Martinelli's scoring: "Everyone's just gonna have to step it up. Definitely losing some scoring from him, so everyone's just got to give it everything they got. We got a lot of shooting this year. The outside shooting is going to be key for us. Spreading the floor, playing faster, guard play… I feel like all around, everyone just got to step it up because that's definitely a big piece that's going to be missed."

Sophomore guard Jake West on the team's incoming transfers: "These guys were super hungry. They're super selfless people. Like Gelo said, they want to show that they belong in the Big Ten, not only to the media but to themselves. Like they made this jump so that they can show that they're ready to compete at the Big Ten level."

West when asked if he has the green light on offense this year: "I think it's super bright. Obviously, last year I didn't really play much at the start of the year and then toward the end of the season, playing 30 minutes a game as a freshman in the Big Ten is not really heard of nowadays. So I think Coach Collins has a lot of confidence in me and my confidence is through the roof as well. I put in so much hard work, keep my faith in God."

West on excitement for the season: "This team is just super hungry to get out there. Obviously, we've been competing in the summer and we've been competing in the preseason against each other, but nothing beats that college basketball atmosphere. Going out there on the road, going out to Welsh-Ryan when it's packed. Like, we're so hungry. We can't wait to play basketball."

West on the importance of returning managers and coaches in helping to instill team culture after a tumultuous offseason: "It's very important to have people that are very invested into the program, right? So obviously we talk about it a lot in practice, but you're only as strong as your weakest link. If you have managers that are messing around, it could affect the program, right? So people that just show up every single day and work very hard — and you guys might think it's funny — but seriously, like a culture starts from people being sharp all the way around, like managers all the way up to head coach. So we've really harped on this year being very sharp, like Gelo said, working very hard and making sure that everything we do is sharp."

West about Symon Ghai: "He's awesome, he's a great dude. He works super hard. Symon works super, super hard. You know, he might mess up a few drills here and there, but you can just tell like he wants it so bad. He works so hard and I think Gelo can attest to playing with him in practice. He might be the only one that's blocked a couple of Gelo's dunks. But he just has so much fresh energy in the locker room and he's always bringing it every day. And like I said before, he doesn't really have any off days. He always has energy."

Head coach Chris Collins on building the roster: "When I woke up one morning and there was only three guys on the roster, it really gave me and my staff an opportunity to get together and say, 'The slate is somewhat clean, let's try to figure out what we want to do with this and how we want to build this roster.'"

Collins on how the roster has meshed in the offseason: "They've been great… the guys have gotten along really well. The chemistry's good. The vibes are good. All the intangible things that I value have been really good so far with this group."

Collins on the team's mentality: "I think there's an inherent chip on the shoulder that a lot of these guys carry, and really, that's who we've been. Even our great players, in my time, three of the most recent most prominent players we've had — Boo Buie, Brooks Barnhizer, Nick Martinelli — not any of those guys had a Big Ten offer coming out of high school. They all became league players and two of them were drafted and are in the NBA now. So, we've always wanted guys that carry a little bit of a chip on their shoulder that believe they can compete against the best. I see that in some of these guys we've brought in: that they're anxious. They're older guys that have done really well in so-called lesser leagues and now they get an opportunity as veteran players to see how they can stack up against the best. There is a hunger, there is a little bit of a chip there."

Collins on hopes for the team despite roster turnover: "Look at that Iowa team, right? I know a lot of those guys played together for coach McCollum, but everybody said those were guys who played at Drake and before that played at Northwest Missouri, and they transferred well when they came in and they ended up going to a tournament, getting to an Elite Eight. So I think there's examples of teams. I thought Nebraska was very much like that last year as well. So, I think we would love to be a team of that mold: tough competitive guys who play really well together. Competitive, and have a good chemistry and hunger to us."

Collins on what the NCAA Tournament's expansion means for Northwestern: "If you come in the top half of the Big Ten, you're going to most likely be in the tournament. It's really hard to win in our league, especially on the road, so I think the expansion will help. That's the way I look at it… now it's just about getting to the tournament. There's so much parity now and it's about matchups and who's playing well at the right time. As long as you can get in there and have a chance to play, you can compete."

Collins on the offseason and the importance of the team's three returners: "Like you said, it's been wild. The spring has become chaotic now with roster construction. We went from three to 12 players in the span of like two weeks. But [the returners] were very instrumental in the recruitment of all these guys. They were very present, whether it be text messages, talking to the guys on the phone, spending time with them on their visits, kind of getting to know them."

Collins on what to expect from a Martinelli-less offense: "I think what you're going to see stylistically is a little bit different, especially offensively, because Nick was such a dominant offensive player. But, you guys know from following us, [Nick] was very unique. In order to play to his skillset, you had to play a certain way, right? He played in isolation a lot and you had to give him space to do what he could do and get the double teams and find open shooters. I think you're going to see a little bit more movement with this year's team. Cutting, a little bit more off ball activity with screening actions: that's going to lend itself more to our team."

Collins on the offense's strengths: "Shooting is something, hopefully, that'll be a real strength for us. I think the guard play, the creativity of Jake and LA Pratt, I think those are going to be two guys that have the ability to play in pick-and-rolls and kind of make plays off that end. Jack Karasinski is really good coming off screens, playing and movement, scoring that. Alex Kostić can really shoot the ball. Angelo Ciaravino is a guy who works well cutting, moving, curling into the lane. He's improved as a shooter. I think that being said, though, I think we have pretty good size. Last year we only had one guy 6-foot-10 and above, now we have four. We have some bigger wings: Jayden Hodge, Colin Smith, Jack Karasinski, Angelo Ciaravino… I think our guards are bigger. Last year, we had three guards that were smaller than Jake West. Now Jake's the smallest guy."

Iowa head coach Ben McCollum about his transfer portal philosophy: "We had 10 returners, which was nice. I would say your best transfers are the guys in your program. So we want to recruit from within and really develop the guys that are currently on our roster and we're hopeful that we've done that. I would say ultimately the best teams, obviously Michigan was pretty unique with their transfer portal class, some of the better teams that consistently win, your UConns and what not… Duke. Like those teams still are pretty heavy high school for the most part. I think that's still what our strength needs to be: developing and recruiting high school kids, keeping them here for as long as you can keep them here."

McCollum on what Iowa's Elite Eight run means for the program going forward: "I mean the job's nowhere near done. I don't think in terms of that, so it's easy for me. I think in terms of trying to build a program and trying to get it to be able to sustain the amount of success that you want. When people come to our practices, they can feel it and they can feel welcomed and established."

Michigan State head coach Tom Izzo when asked about his strength as a coach: "We all got something, you know. Painter… his best strength is he finds seven-four guys that are bigger than God and they're really good. And he makes them good, but everybody's got his strength. And my only strength that I think I have is some time for my players."

Izzo when asked about where he's at with retirement: "I'm right in front of you, brother. So the million dollar question, 'when are you gonna retire?' When I don't have the energy, when the bad things outweigh the good things. And I said this 100 times and I'll say it one more: I still love my job, love the practices, love the meetings, love the film sessions. I do not respect my profession as much as I should right now, but I've been on every board trying to change it. I want to keep trying to change it… I'm good to go, man. If you come next year, you might see me again."

Izzo about high expectations for Jeremy Fears Jr.: "Fortunately, I've been here long enough that we've had a lot of time for it. When expectations have been high for a player, it's always a little different. But I think he's been through some things that help him stay grounded. I will say this, this summer I thought he had one of the best summers he's ever had there. And I have not seen, the four letter word that — you know, there's a lot of four letter words I use and I can't use here — and one that's as bad as any of them is entitlement. And I think we're getting a lot of people entitled and he has not shown any of the entitlement and that's what excites me the most."

USC guard Rodney Rice when asked about USC's goal for the season: "Win a national championship."

USC forward Jacob Cofie on the strength of USC's roster: "I would say our lineups, how many different lineups we could run, how deep our team is. I feel like everyone on our team can play, to be honest with you. We have a lot of height and length, so I think we'll use it as an advantage for us and I think that'll bring us together as a team."

Illinois head coach Brad Underwood when asked about expanding college basketball to the summer: "Yeah, but I don't want it in the summer. Summer's an awful idea. I'm not in favor of that at all. I think that's getting the cart before the horse. I think we need to expand the regular season. I think we need to grow the regular season. We need to play more games. We need to play more meaningful games."

Underwood on expanding the regular season: "I just don't think we can make basketball a year-round sport. And I don't want to see us do that and then have to go back and change it because in five or whatever years we change the schedule and we're playing more games and whatever. And I do think we need to play more games. We need to play 40, 45, whatever."

Underwood on the state of college basketball and the Protect College Sports Act that would create legislation surrounding NIL, the transfer portal and eligibility: "We need help. The game of basketball has never been better than it is right now and we shouldn't move aside of that. But we need more structure, we need regulation. We need help. The Big Ten's in favor of that, the conferences are in favor of that. I hope we can get the House support that we need for that to pass. It's obviously gone through the Senate. But college sports needs that. We can't continue to stay unregulated with this Wild West mentality. We need that."

Indiana head coach Darian DeVries on if Michigan winning a championship lowers expectations for his team: "No, it doesn't change anything at all. Our challenge is being the best version of Indiana we can be. So, all this, it doesn't really matter. Like last year and the year before, 10 years ago, our goal right now is for us to go challenge for a Big Ten Championship, challenge to make a deep run in the NCAA Tournament."

DeVries on his hopes for Indiana's identity: "Physical, tough. That's what we have to be. And that's what we try to recruit to. It's our approach every day in practice. We want physical, tough, to be good at the things that can be prioritized, taking care of the basketball. You've got to be physical and tough, take care of the basketball. Defensive, offensive rebounding."

Nebraska head coach Fred Hoiberg on the high expectations for the program that have come following the team's success last season: "You talk about expectations, that's why you're in this thing. You don't want to go into a season every year where you're picked at the bottom, the bottom third or whatever it is. You want those expectations. You want to live up to them. We talked about that. We are the hunted this year, where we were picked where we are. Last year, we had a chip on our shoulder and used that as motivation. You can't lose that, even though you got picked much higher than you were a year ago."

UCLA head coach Mick Cronin on the Big Ten: "Big Ten basketball is hard, very hard. It's hard to win. Great players, great coaches, great road environments. The actual game is played with hard guys that play hard. Guys that are big, tough, strong, hard guys. It's not for the weak, Big Ten basketball. It's the depth of our conference, it's the depth. In our conference, teams eight through 13 play in the tournament or have played int the tournament. It's not easy to get a win and it's real easy to get off track in this league."

Cronin on the transfer portal and player retention: "Well recruiting and retention, as far as player acquisition, is all about money. So it's easier for some people — those that have more money — it's harder for those that don't. And look there's people out there that said we retained all five guys. Now, if you say, well you're in Westwood: UCLA tradition… No, no we paid them. We paid the five guys that we retained, that were the five guys that had eligibility left on our team, but we paid them."

Cronin on the importance of money in getting players: "Most guys leave predominantly in this era for more money. Some leave for more opportunity and more money. Of course, relationships matter. You have to have relationships, and [money has] never been more important than having a relationship. But what I'm trying tell you, there are coaches, some in this league, that have great relationships with their players and they still have a league because they got four times the amount of money. And I'm not gonna name names, but there's coaches where you'll say, 'Well, you know, this guy does a great job.' It's just a comedy show when a kid commits to a school and says, 'He really bonded with the staff,' and he met [them] two weeks ago… but nobody wants to say that. It's okay. That's how free agency goes. There's nothing wrong with it, but we really got to talk about the truth. The reason the guy left a team at a bottom of the Power Five — that was their best player — is because he got three times more money to go to the best team. It's just the facts. Some guys got no chance. They can't retain their players. It's tough, it's tough, it's hard on them. Fortunately, I'm not in that situation, I'm selling hamburgers down on Santa Monica Boulevard."

Washington head coach Danny Sprinkle on Washington's financial outlook: "Once we get a full share [of Big Ten funding], I think it's in 2030, that'll help our program immensely. From a fundraising standpoint, everything. The Big Ten's the best of the best and now you're going in there with a half share, that's hard. I give our athletic director Pat Chun and just our athletic department a lot of credit for the way that we've handled things and still been able to compete."

Oregon forward Andrew Meadows on the team learning about Dana Altman's retirement: "It was just out of the blue. We were really surprised. Honestly, I didn't know what it was going to be because we finished our scrimmage in the morning yesterday and then he pulled us in the film room. I thought it was going to be like maybe some new shoes or something and then he gave us the news."

Meadows on Altman's message to the team: "His message yesterday was that he's excited for us and that we have to stay together. We can't let this break us apart. I think from the vibes in the locker room yesterday, after we all went back in, we're a very motivated group. We have a lot of talent. Our teammates are very talented players. We all have a chip on our shoulder. We all want to win."

articles.title: Bo Nix Admits Broncos ‘Let a Teammate Down’ After Sean Payton’s Major Decision
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos struggled again on offense, leading head coach Sean Payton to take over playcalling duties. Quarterback Bo Nix responded with an honest ad...
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos struggled again on offense, leading head coach Sean Payton to take over playcalling duties. Quarterback Bo Nix responded with an honest admission, saying the players let offensive coordinator Davis Webb down by failing to execute and support him.

The sudden shift hands playcalling back to an experienced head coach while putting the burden squarely on the roster to turn their season around.

Sean Payton takes back playcalling duties after four games

Payton confirmed Thursday that he is taking play-calling duties back from first-year offensive coordinator Webb after only four games. He handed Webb the call sheet in February after calling plays himself in each of his 18 previous seasons as a head coach.

The decision came with a message from the locker room. "Sean Payton said Bo Nix was disappointed in Davis Webb losing play calling because the offense feels like they let a teammate down," Stevens wrote .

Former Broncos receiver Brandon Stokley first reported the move Wednesday night on Broncos Sports Radio 104.3, and ESPN's Adam Schefter described it as a more collaborative approach in which Webb keeps a significant game-planning role. "We'll make a change offensively," Payton said. "I'll call the plays." He also praised his coordinator. "I've done this long enough where I know when I have a future head coach, and Webb's gonna be one."

The Broncos are 2-2 after a 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on October 4. Webb's first game as play-caller ended in a 31-10 loss at Kansas City on September 14, a game in which the Broncos gained only 176 yards.

Bo Nix says offense left coordinator in difficult spot

The Broncos offense has stalled through four games. The Broncos rank 27th in the NFL in points per game (18.5) and yards per game (280.3), and their 13 first-half points are the fewest in the league. Against San Francisco, 29 of Nix's 42 attempts went behind the line of scrimmage or less than 10 yards downfield.

A reporter asked Bo Nix whether the offense let Webb down, and his answer was direct. Nix said , "Absolutely. I think players didn't make it easy on him. Pretty pitiful, actually. … We called exactly what we prepared and what we wanted to get, and we just didn't execute, and then we were behind. I don't think we did a whole lot of good consistently to win the game. " Ahead of the upcoming matchup, Payton made it clear that his young quarterback remains fully supportive of the coaching staff.

Nix has not turned on his coordinator. "I'm real confident in him," he said after that game.

articles.title: Three players, two matchups, and one prediction for Virginia football vs. Syracuse
articles.summary: The ’Hoos need to steady the ship against the Orange.
articles.body:
The vibes couldn't have been higher for Virginia football after its first two games. The 'Hoos dominated NC State in a season-opening statement and took care of business against an overmatched Norfolk State squad. Virginia was ranked, confident, and primed to make another run at the ACC Championship game.

Then the 'Hoos went to Charlotte. Then they went to Tallahassee. And just three short weeks later, the sky is officially falling in Hooville.

After getting waxed, 38-7, by Florida State last weekend, Virginia (3-2, 1-1 ACC) returns home looking to steady the ship against a Syracuse Orange (2-2, 0-2 ACC) squad that, on paper, wouldn't have struck fear into the 'Hoos before the season began. But the season has very much begun, and you never know what you'll get from a team in freefall.

Was last weekend's butt-whooping a wake-up call or the beginning of an unexpectedly long season? Saturday will go a long way in answering that question. So, to get you set for a hinge point in Virginia's season, here are three Syracuse players to know, two matchups to watch, and one prediction for Saturday's matchup.

Starting quarterback Steve Angeli was benched after throwing just one touchdown and five interceptions in two Orange losses to California and Pittsburgh, opening the door for Kennesaw State transfer Amari Odom to take the reins. Syracuse named Odom the starter just before kickoff against UConn last Saturday, and the senior from Inglewood, California, quickly proved he was the right call. Odom completed 73% of his passes for 335 yards and five touchdowns, and he added another score on the ground as the Orange escaped a shootout with a 42-41 overtime win over the rival Huskies.

After a performance of that caliber, Odom seems to have the QB1 job for now, but the injury report is muddying the waters. Odom was last listed as questionable on Thursday with arm/shoulder soreness, which could give Angeli another shot.

The injury makes Saturday a difficult scout for Virginia, as Odom offers much more dual-threat capability — 347 rushing yards and seven TDs last season at Kennesaw State — compared to Angeli, who has -20 career rushing yards.

A Woodbridge, Virginia, native, wide receiver Umari Hatcher is the clear-cut top receiving option for the Orange. With 29 receptions for 434 yards and five touchdowns through four games, Hatcher has more receiving yards than the next three top Syracuse pass-catchers combined.

After pulling in 12 catches for 153 yards and three scores against UConn last week, Hatcher has earned his way onto the Biletnikoff Award Watch List and should be at the top of Virginia's defensive scouting report.

UT Martin transfer linebacker Keyshawn Johnson has made an immediate impact against higher-level competition. Though slightly undersized at 6-foot-3 and 230 pounds, Johnson leads the Orange with 3.5 sacks and already has a forced fumble, a fumble recovery, and a pass breakup on his 2026 stat sheet.

Johnson has a clearly defined role in the Orange defense: get after the quarterback. And after allowing 10 sacks against the Seminoles last weekend, Johnson needs to be circled and highlighted on the Virginia scouting report.

Virginia's offensive line vs. the Syracuse pass rush

Aside from Keyshawn Johnson, Syracuse's pass rush isn't particularly scary, and frankly, it would be discouraging to see the Orange generate any consistent pressure on Beau Pribula this Saturday.

Virginia's offensive line, lauded before the season for its age and experience, didn't show up against Florida State, allowing 10 sacks and pressure in the backfield on nearly every play. The 'Hoos need, and should get, a major bounce-back effort inside Scott Stadium against the Orange.

The Syracuse rushing attack vs. Virginia's defense

The 'Hoos were gashed for 281 rushing yards by the Seminoles last weekend, highlighted by a 136-yard, five-touchdown rushing effort by quarterback Ashton Daniels. Virginia put one of the worst tackling displays you'll ever see on tape as the Seminoles ripped off explosive run after explosive run.

Now, Virginia will welcome a Syracuse offense that ranks sixth in the ACC with 166.3 rushing yards per game heading into the weekend. The 'Hoos could catch a break if Odom can't suit up, as we've seen what can happen to the defense against a mobile quarterback, but regardless of who's under center, Virginia needs to be more disciplined against the Orange.

Are the 'Hoos who we thought they were through two games? Evidently not. But I'm not willing to accept just yet that Virginia has completely forgotten how to play football. Syracuse was projected to finish 12 th in the ACC Preseason Poll, and after losses to Pittsburgh and California, the Orange has done little to discredit that ranking.

Virginia fans are yearning for a glimpse of the dominant rushing attack that flashed in the season opener against NC State. At home against a Syracuse defense that just gave up 41 points to UConn is as favorable a spot as any to reignite the ground game.

As long as the 'Hoos aren't the victim of an Amari Odom-led Syracuse magic carpet ride, I think Virginia, which is nearly a touchdown favorite, gets back on track. I'm ready to get hurt again, so give me the 'Hoos by 10.

Score prediction: Virginia 28, Syracuse 18

articles.title: Josh McDaniels described Patriots' offensive line with one word
articles.summary: Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels has been impressed with the way the offensive line has adjusted after injuries early in the season.
articles.body:
New England Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels had one word to describe his offensive line after a big victory over the Buffalo Bills last week.

It's a resilient unit that has struggled at times through the first four games of the season. They are down to their third option at right guard due to injuries, and right tackle Morgan Moses has been banged up. Still, the unit held off the Bills for the team's best offensive performance of the season.

With extra time, quarterback Drake Maye got comfortable and was more deliberate with his decision-making on the field. He outdueled Bills quarterback Josh Allen by going 22-of-37 passing for 269 yards, three touchdowns and one interception, along with eight rushes for 54 yards on the ground.

The Patriots ran 76 total offensive snaps, which was their highest total in a single game this season. Much of their success was due to the improvements along the offensive line.

"Fighters," McDaniels responded, when describing the offensive line, via Patriots Wire's Sophie Weller.

The Patriots will have their work cut out in maintaining that mentality for Sunday's clash with star edge rusher Maxx Crosby and the Las Vegas Raiders' defense.

Crosby is a game-wrecker capable of creating havoc in the Patriots' offensive backfield. But as shown against the Bills, Maye and the offense could do the same if the offensive line wins in the trenches and gives him time to scan and process the field.

Follow Patriots Wire on Twitter and Facebook .
