articles.title: Why Edgerrin Cooper’s absence is a big deal
articles.summary: Off-ball linebackers are considered the least valuable defensive players. What my post presupposes is maybe they are.
articles.body:
It's easy to understand that Green Bay Packers off-ball linebacker Edgerrin Cooper was (and still likely is) a budding star, and an incredibly important player for the Packers. You don't need any fancy numbers or a scout's eye to pick him out, he's the kind of player that just looks different. Even among professional athletes, he's faster, lighter on his feet, and changes direction in a way that seems to defy physics.

Cooper also plays a position that is often looked down on by analysts as the least "valuable" part of the defense. Like running backs on offense, most teams (not the Packers, mind you) are able to field at least competent running backs without difficulty. The "off ball" linebacker is not directly in control of pressuring the quarterback or covering receivers, and while they are important, they play a secondary support role.

The problem with wedging Edgerrin Cooper into this analysis is that the reason you can generally find a competent linebacker is because that other positions CAN serve to cover many of their responsibilities. (Emphasis on can.) Good safeties can reduce the field they are responsible for in pass coverage. Good defensive linemen can create clear lanes for them in run support. Good edge rushers can occupy multiple blockers, leaving them free to shoot up field and bring people down. And in doing so, they can allow a linebacker to play to his strengths. The well-liked veteran Zaire Franklin is this kind of linebacker, and honestly, he's a great running mate for Cooper. Franklin is smart, he's generally in the right position, and he's a sure tackler, but he's slow and can be exploited in pass defense.

To put it simply, for most teams the play of the non-linebackers can allow that team to get away with lesser linebackers. However, with Cooper, the exact opposite is true. Cooper allowed the Packers to get away with lesser players at other every other position AND allowed the good players and stars at other positions to focus on what they do best. Without him, every edge rusher and corner will have to focus more on tasks that they would prefer not to be bothered with. Zaire Franklin will have to cover more than he (or the Packers) would like. Evan Williams and Xavier McKinney will have to worry just a bit more about the space in front of them. Every time a tight end is split out wide, someone will have to make a decision that they previously did not have to make.

Green Bay has had an extremely rough few seasons so far losing lynchpins, going back to Micah Parsons. All teams suffer injuries, but few have endured quite so many "domino effect" losses. The Packers spent the last two weeks valiantly attempting to repair their interior offensive line by signing three veterans, only to have another big leak spring on defense. They did not have a ton of depth in the first place, and Cooper is one of the least replaceable players on the team. The Bears will, at least be starting backup quarterback Tyson Bagent, but even so, the Packers face a tall task on defense going forward.

articles.title: Max Homa Chases First Win Since 2023 In Japan
articles.summary: Max Homa sits two shots back at the Baycurrent Classic, looking to break a winless streak that began after the 2023 Farmers Insurance Open.
articles.body:
Max Homa stands on the brink of ending a long drought on the PGA Tour. The American is currently in contention at the Baycurrent Classic in Japan, sitting just two shots off the lead after the second round. This moment matters deeply for a player who once held the fifth spot in the world rankings but has struggled to find his footing since the 2023 Ryder Cup in Italy. At Yokohama Country Club on Friday, Homa shot a 68 that was 3-under par, bringing his total to 9-under par. He joins a tight group of competitors, but the pressure is mounting to finally get back into the winner's circle. The last time he held a trophy was the 2023 Farmers Insurance Open, and the clock has been ticking ever since.

The leaderboard at the halfway mark tells a clear story of who is in the hunt. As reported by GolfMagic, Keith Mitchell and Jacob Bridgeman share the top spot at 11-under par. Mitchell shot a 6-under 65 on Friday, while Bridgeman posted a 68 to go with his opening 63. The two leaders held a two-shot advantage over a group containing Homa. The American was part of a four-man cluster at 9-under, which also featured Ben Kohles, Mac Meissner, and Zach Bauchou. Kohles actually fired the low round of the day with a 62, but he remains in the same position as Homa on the board. Justin Thomas, Stephan Jaeger, and Min Woo Lee are one shot further back at 8-under. Among the 13 of the 24 players from the Presidents Cup held in the Chicago suburbs just two weeks ago, the field is strong. Hideki Matsuyama, the top star from Japan, shot a 1-over 72 and sits eight shots off the lead. Despite the high level of competition, Homa's game plan seems to be working. He has managed to stay within striking distance despite the pressure of the chase.

Homa has always found a special connection with the fans in Japan, and that energy appears to be a key factor in his current form. He knows the course and the atmosphere well, often making this trip a priority on his calendar. During a previous visit, he explained his love for the location with a simple statement: "I love it over here. It's always on my schedule." He also noted that the vibe of the place seems to unlock something in his game, saying, "I love Japan. I think just the energy here just helps me play a little bit better for some reason." This confidence was on display during his Friday round. He faced a tricky stretch but kept his head down. As he put it, "Had a really weird like 40 minutes out there around 14, but just happy I didn't try to reinvent the wheel or anything, I was playing well." His ability to stick to his game plan when things get weird is exactly what a veteran needs to close out a tournament. He didn't panic, and that discipline is what keeps him in the hunt.

The battle for the title will intensify as the tournament moves into the weekend. With only two shots separating the leaders from the chasing pack, every stroke on Saturday and Sunday will count. Homa needs to maintain his focus and avoid the mistakes that have plagued him over the last two seasons. The final round is set to take place on Sunday, October 11, at the Yokohama Country Club.

articles.title: Commanders announce great Jayden Daniels news for Week 5 Giants matchup
articles.summary: This is some incredible news for the Commanders and their star quarterback.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders lost to the Indianapolis Colts in Week 4, and it was thanks in part to being without Terry McLaurin and the early injury to Marcus Mariota.

Unfortunately, Mariota is going to miss some time, which is why the recent news about Jayden Daniels is so great and comes at the perfect time for Washington.

Commanders' head coach Dan Quinn announced Friday that Daniels, after missing Weeks 3 and 4, will be the Week 5 starter against the New York Giants on Sunday.

Commanders announce Jayden Daniels as starting QB for Week 5 vs. Giants

"HC Dan Quinn confirmed that Jayden Daniels will start on Sunday," the Commanders announced on social media Friday afternoon.

This is some massive news for the Commanders, though it's not totally unexpected. All week, the signs were pointing towards Daniels being active and starting for the Commanders in Week 5.

But hearing the confirmation from the head coach, all doubt can be put aside. The Commanders, for the first time since the first half of Week 2, will have their star quarterback back on the field.

He'll be playing with a brace on his left arm to protect his left elbow, which was dislocated at the end of the first half against the Dallas Cowboys a few weeks ago.

Daniels opted against surgery and is trying to come back and play this season, pushing surgery, which would likely have knocked him out for the season, to the offseason.

He might not be at full strength for Washington this weekend, especially against a tricky Giants team in possibly bad weather conditions.

But regardless of how things go, it's still a huge boost of confidence for the Commanders to get their starting quarterback back this season.

articles.title: MVSU’s Qingfang Pang becomes third college basketball player recently detained by ICE
articles.summary: Mississippi Valley State forward Qingfang Pang was detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) last week and is currently in custody, according to...
articles.body:
Mississippi Valley State forward Qingfang Pang was detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) last week and is currently in custody, according to the ICE locator database .

Pang, a 6-foot-9 forward from the People's Republic of China, was trying to fly from Jackson, Mississippi to New York, where his American visa sponsor is, his attorney Marcus Session told Front Office Sports. Pang's lawyer says that he was detained due to an expired visa, and he told local TV that Pang "didn't know his visa was expired."

Pang is one of two Chinese players on the Delta Devils roster. He is a transfer from Monroe University in New York, where he averaged 7.3 points and 3.8 rebounds per game over the last two seasons. He attended high school at Christ the King in New York City and was once recruited by high-major programs during his high school career.

"Mississippi Valley State University is aware of the situation involving one of our students and is deeply concerned for the student's well-being," MVSU said in a statement on Thursday. "The student is registered as a full-time student at Mississippi Valley State University. University officials are closely monitoring the situation and are committed to providing appropriate support as circumstances develop."

Known college basketball players in ICE custody

He is at least the third college basketball player to be detained by ICE in recent months. Kentucky State women's basketball player Amina Seck was released this week after two months in detention. Southern Connecticut State men's player Deng Deng was released 12 days after he was detained in September.

ICE arrests have skyrocketed during the second Trump administration. According to the Prison Policy Initiative, there was a nearly 3x increase in ICE arrests in 2025 from 2024, with over 300,000 arrests made, and that number is only growing again in 2026. Meanwhile, college basketball is a more global game than ever, with a growing international presence.

Mississippi Valley State opens up its season against Oklahoma on November 6. It plays against 10 high-major opponents on the road in non-conference play, and doesn't play a home game until January 9. It is unclear when and if Pang will be able to rejoin the team.

articles.title: Class Of 2027 Prospect Akol Nyok Commits To Marquette Men’s Basketball
articles.summary: The top 100-ish big man is the third commitment in the class for the Golden Eagles.
articles.body:
Marquette men's basketball and head coach Shaka Smart have picked up a new commitment for the Class of 2027. Akol Nyok has joined Marlon Martinez and Philipe Ndong as the future of the Golden Eagles.

247 Sports lists Nyok as a 7'1", 205 pound center. He attends Columbus High School, which is in Miami, Florida. 247 rates Nyok as a four-star prospect and ranks him at #101 in their internal system. He's #103 in the 247 Sports Composite rankings, and the 13th best center prospect in the country. On3/Rivals matches the four-star rating and ranks Nyok waaaaaay up at #70 internally. That boost him up to #92 in the Rivals Industry rankings, which is their version of a composite ranking. ESPN has him somewhere outside the top 100 as they don't rank Nyok, but he is a four-star prospect in their eyes. ESPN also says he's the 13th best center prospect in the country, and since they have 12 centers in the top 100 , Nyok can't be that far outside the top 100, right?

Based on the last few things listed on Nyok's 247 Sports page , it would seem that this recruitment came down to Marquette and Virginia Tech. He visited the Golden Eagles back in late July and then stopped off in Blacksburg in mid-September . Those are his only two visits logged going back to October 2023, and they came amidst scholarship offers from Michigan State and Maryland. That list isn't perfect of course, as our friends over at A Sea Of Blue noted Kentucky offering Nyok a scholarship back in early September .

If you wanted to be a particular way about it, you could absolutely say that Marquette just beat out Kentucky on the recruiting trail.

Nyok is an extremely mobile seven-footer with glaring defensive tools. He runs the floor like a gazelle, is a quality rim protector (1.6 per game in Pro16 play), and can also guard on the perimeter. He's unusually twitchy for a player his size, enabling him to react quickly as plays evolve, and be very versatile, both in terms of ball-screen coverages and even being somewhat switchable. Nyok is also a very good help defender who tracks the ball throughout the possession and is proactive helping, instead of just waiting for the ball at the rim. That's part of why he's not a more impactful defensive rebounder (4.1 per game), but his lack of strength and inconsistent hands also play a part. Physically, he's very lean right now and not only needs to build-up his body, but also prove his durability. His offense is behind his defense right now and a lot of that boils down to hands and balance as well. It's not that he shies away from contact – In fact, he's actually a willing screener, not just on the ball but even with Gortats against would-be help-side defenders – but that he struggles to hold his ground when his base isn't under him. He's a definite rim-runner and vertical spacer, but otherwise ends up laying balls in he should dunk because of questionable timing and an inconsistent ability to grab, and hold onto, balls. He is, however, a very active offensive rebounder (3.9 per game), but not a scoring threat away from the basket. He's not only a low percentage free-throw shooter (53%), but gets their seldomly (1.9 attempts per game). The bottom line is that Nyok needs time to build-up his frame and improve his hands, but he has the size, mobility, and motor to be a major factor on the defensive end of the floor and simultaneously a specific offensive niche as a rim-runner and lob threat.

Nyok is an extremely mobile seven-footer with glaring defensive tools. He runs the floor like a gazelle, is a quality rim protector (1.6 per game in Pro16 play), and can also guard on the perimeter. He's unusually twitchy for a player his size, enabling him to react quickly as plays evolve, and be very versatile, both in terms of ball-screen coverages and even being somewhat switchable. Nyok is also a very good help defender who tracks the ball throughout the possession and is proactive helping, instead of just waiting for the ball at the rim. That's part of why he's not a more impactful defensive rebounder (4.1 per game), but his lack of strength and inconsistent hands also play a part. Physically, he's very lean right now and not only needs to build-up his body, but also prove his durability.

His offense is behind his defense right now and a lot of that boils down to hands and balance as well. It's not that he shies away from contact – In fact, he's actually a willing screener, not just on the ball but even with Gortats against would-be help-side defenders – but that he struggles to hold his ground when his base isn't under him. Here's 7 minutes of highlights that just got posted in early September.

And now, the brand new scholarship/roster chart, and then a discussion of what you're seeing in there.

See the big ol' red line in between Philipe Ndong and Akol Nyok? That's because Marquette currently projects to have 16 players on their roster in 2027-28, and the roster limit is 15. The Golden Eagles currently project as one over the limit, and I want to be clear about this: I don't care about the fact that they're projecting as not having enough space for the players on the roster to return and the freshmen to come aboard next summer.

What I care about is the fact that we can all look at the 2025-26 season and the 2026-27 roster and see at least three players that we can all have zero expectation to contribute to the Golden Eagles in 26-27 and also have eligibility to return for 2027-28. I don't know why they're on the roster now, and the fact that head coach Shaka Smart is accepting Nyok's commitment means he already knows they're not going to be here next year. If we're pretty comfortable with the idea that they can't contribute now AND they won't be here next year, why are they here now?

Two of the players I'm referring to have eligibility that extends into the 2028-29 season, and you will notice that Marquette does not project to have an open roster spot in that campaign either as a result of Nyok's commitment. Again, I don't care about that aspect of it. I care about dragging around players that don't have a present value to the program and the program is very clearly signaling that they don't have a future, either. This is all going to get settled one way or another, and by the time we tip off in November 2027, none of this will matter.

But for now, in October 2026, we have to ask serious questions about how things are being managed.

articles.title: SEC considering restoring archaic transfer policy
articles.summary: This would be a brutal development for the SEC.
articles.body:
Here we go again. The drama just does not stop. It's a cycle that never seems to end. Rules get made, and then they change… and then they revert back.

According to sources telling On3 , the SEC is considering restoring a transfer policy that would require intraconference athletes to sit out a year before playing for another conference school.

Okay, for real, why does it matter if an athlete transfers in-conference or not? Seriously, why does it matter? If we're going to let athletes transfer, why does it matter if they transfer to a school that's also in the conference? Not only is that ridiculous, but it would likely take talent away from the SEC.

This all started in 2021, when the NCAA allowed players to transfer one time without penalty, before that changed in 2024 to allow multiple transfers without penalty. The SEC followed suit in 2021, which included players being able to transfer within the conference without penalty.

One SEC school source raised the concern to On3 that restoring the transfer policy would put SEC schools at a competitive disadvantage by not being able to add talent from the conference in the portal.

The college football transfer portal does not officially open until January, but general managers and agents told On3 they expect retention talks to begin in earnest in the next two to four weeks. When the regular season wraps up at the end of November, programs will know the status of nearly everyone on their roster and which players are expected to enter the portal.

"We're running into this crazy world where if I don't talk to a guy's agent on the bye week, they're saying, 'You didn't want to get him back,'" an SEC front-office staffer recently told On3. "And I'm like, 'How is that possible? No, I just didn't want to distract him in the middle of the season.' It's coming, it's coming soon."

What a world we live in. And good on the front-office staffer for not wanting to distract a player during the bye week.

Kentucky has players including Nic Anderson, Jordan Castell, Aaron Gates, Lance Heard, and Olaus Allen who transferred from SEC schools this past offseason. Imagine what this team would look like right now without those guys.

articles.title: Will Ja'Marr Chase play against the Dolphins? What we know
articles.summary: Bengals receiver Ja'Marr Chase was in uniform at practice Friday ahead of the team's NFL Week 5 game in Miami.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals receiver Ja'Marr Chase was in uniform at practice Friday ahead of the team's NFL Week 5 game against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium.

Chase is listed as questionable on the team's injury report, per Bengals head coach Zac Taylor.

One day earlier, Chase was in uniform and going through team stretch as well as sprints during practice.

Photos: Bengals vs. Jaguars on Sunday October 4

Taylor said Oct. 7 that Chase remains in concussion protocol and was being monitored day-to-day.

Taylor said Monday that Chase was considered "day to day," but could be in concussion protocol for most or all of the week.

Chase's teammate, Tee Higgins, was not dressed in uniform for practice for the second consecutive day because of an adductor injury he suffered in a Week 4 loss to Jacksonville.

Earlier in the week, Taylor said Chase was in concussion protocol after leaving the game against Jacksonville during the second quarter and not returning .

Chase went to the locker room for evaluation for a concussion, and the Bengals announced his return as questionable. As the second half started, the Bengals ruled out Chase 's return.

After a four-yard catch from quarterback Joe Burrow , Chase had his facemask grabbed by Jaguars defensive back Jarrian Jones . Chase went to the ground and took a big hit from linebacker Ventrell Miller.

Jones drew a 15-yard penalty. Miller was not penalized. CBS analyst Robert Turbin said he couldn't believe Miller didn't draw a flag.

"I'm still really shocked there was no foul called on that play leading with the crown of his helmet," Turbin said during the third quarter of the broadcast.

Near the end of the first half, Turbin and play-by-play announcer Tom McCarthy said they were surprised Jones wasn't penalized for pass interference on a long pass attempt from Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow to Higgins, who was injured later in the game.

articles.body:
Resilience and forward pressure carried Khundet PK Saenchai to a majority decision win over Kiwthong TKD Muaythai in their bantamweight Muay Thai co-main event clash at ONE Friday Fights 174 in Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok, Thailand, on Friday, October 9.

It was all gas and no brakes from the opening bell of this Asia primetime fixture, with Kiwthong breaking through his foe with right hands down the middle. The 21-year-old PK Saenchai Muaythaigym representative tried to break through in return, but the former used push kicks to launch him across the ring.

The telling moment of the opening frame came when both fighters clashed in a fiery exchange, and Khundet pierced Kiwthong's eye with an elbow. Round two got off to a similar start.

Kiwthong hammered in punches from the back foot as Khundet marched forward, chin tucked to his chest, absorbing the shots. Once the PK Saenchai Muaythaigym product closed the distance, a right hand laid Kiwthong down. He, however, made the count and survived the stanza.

In the third canto, Khundet came out looking for the finish. But the durable 21-year-old Kiwthong kept sending hands back, ripping punches to the body and head that made the Thai wilt. Neither man folded entirely under the pressure, trading at full intensity until the final bell.

In the end, two of the three judges sided with Khundet, who earned his 65th win.

articles.title: New York Giants vs. Washington Commanders: 5 players to start/sit for fantasy football in Week 5
articles.summary: Here's a look at some start/sit decisions for fantasy football in the Week 5 matchup between the New York Giants and Washington Commanders.
articles.body:
The New York Giants (3-1) will look to continue their hot start to the 2026 season when they travel to take on the Washington Commanders (1-3) in Week 5.

The Giants enter Sunday's matchup with a 3-1 record after picking up back-to-back wins over the Tennessee Titans and Arizona Cardinals. Washington, meanwhile, is 1-3 following last week's 30-13 loss to the Indianapolis Colts in London.

New York holds the top spot in the division alone for the first time since 2015.

While the Giants have played much better than many expected through the first month of the season, there are plenty of fantasy football questions surrounding Sunday's divisional matchup.

There are some injury notes to keep an eye on. Malik Nabers is dealing with a knee injury, Cam Skattebo is nursing a shoulder injury and Jayden Daniels is expected to return after missing the last two games with an elbow injury.

With that in mind, here are five Giants and Commanders players to start or sit in fantasy football for Week 5.

This one is pretty simple if Nabers is cleared to play. The Giants' No. 1 wide receiver is coming off his best performance of the season, catching six passes for 112 yards and a touchdown on seven targets against the Cardinals.

Nabers also has an extremely favorable matchup against a Washington secondary that has struggled to slow down opposing passing attacks. The Commanders have allowed 12 passing touchdowns through four games, tied for the most in the NFL.

The biggest concern is his knee. Nabers missed Wednesday's practice because of soreness but returned as a limited participant Thursday. His availability will be something to monitor heading into Sunday.

If Nabers is active, he should be in starting lineups.

Isaiah Likely has quickly become one of Jameis Winston's favorite targets, and that should continue against Washington. Likely saw a massive 12 targets in Week 4 and finished with seven receptions for 66 yards. He has now established himself as one of the most heavily involved pass catchers in the Giants' offense.

That makes him especially appealing in PPR formats. Washington has also struggled to defend opposing tight ends, creating another favorable matchup for Likely. Washington has allowed the third-most fantasy points per game to the position.

The Giants are likely to see plenty of zone coverage from Washington, which could give Winston opportunities to find Likely underneath and in the middle of the field.

After missing the last two games with an elbow injury, Daniels is expected to return Sunday against the Giants.

Daniels has played only six quarters this season, but he's already thrown three touchdown passes without an interception while adding 100 rushing yards on 12 carries.

The rushing ability gives Daniels a relatively high fantasy floor, and that could be particularly important against a Giants defense that has generated six interceptions through four games.

New York has done an excellent job limiting opposing quarterbacks from a fantasy perspective, but Daniels brings an element that Cam Ward, Jacoby Brissett and Dak Prescott don't necessarily possess.

Daniels is expected to wear a brace on his injured elbow, but the Commanders have indicated that he is ready to play. Assuming there are no setbacks, Daniels is worth starting as a borderline QB1 option.

Harris has become more involved in the Giants' backfield, but this isn't the week to trust him in fantasy lineups.

Cam Skattebo, who is a starting option by the way, remains the clear lead back, and Harris has been working primarily as the secondary option. Harris has also seen his opportunities fluctuate throughout games, making it difficult to predict exactly how much work he'll receive.

That's especially concerning against a Washington defense that has been much tougher against the run than it has been against the pass. Skattebo has already seen 76 touches this season, while Harris has received a considerably smaller workload. Skattebo's volume makes him the more appealing fantasy option even in a difficult matchup.

Even if you're dealing with significant bye-week or injury problems, Harris belongs on the bench.

McLaurin is another difficult fantasy decision this week, and his injury situation makes it even more complicated.

The veteran wide receiver missed Washington's Week 4 game with a hamstring injury and opened this week without practicing. Even if McLaurin is cleared to play, there are reasons to be cautious.

The Commanders have dealt with significant uncertainty at quarterback and among their receiving corps, and Washington has yet to produce a wide receiver who has finished inside the top 10 at the position this season.

The return of Daniels would certainly help McLaurin's outlook, but expecting him to immediately return to a full workload after dealing with a hamstring injury is risky.

If McLaurin is active and receives a positive pregame report, he becomes more appealing. But even then, he might be best left on the bench to wait and see another week.

articles.title: Kings’ Vivek Ranadive turning fancy dinner with team into a full-blown roast is so KANGZ
articles.summary: The Sacramento Kings had a very difficult end to their last season campaign and ended up with a nightmarish 22-60 record. The team definitely needed a boost...
articles.body:
The Sacramento Kings had a very difficult end to their last season campaign and ended up with a nightmarish 22-60 record. The team definitely needed a boost of motivation coming into the new season after being ousted from playoff contention by the Charlotte Hornets.

However, Vivek Ranadive reportedly used a team dinner to confront players, coaches, and executives about the franchise's struggles .

The speech, however, left some attendees questioning whether his attempt to motivate the organization had gone as planned.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Ringer's Zach Lowe shared the story Thursday on The Zach Lowe Show, explaining that Ranadive addressed the group during a training camp dinner attended by the team and staff.

"They went out to a fancy training [camp] dinner, team, the whole team, the staff, everything," Lowe said. "And at the dinner, Vivek Ranadivé spoke, and he kind of turned the dinner into a roast of lots of people in the room, telling them all the ways in which they have been failing as players, coaches, executives, whatever."

According to Lowe, the reaction was split. Some people reportedly felt the approach was backfiring, while others believed Ranadive was trying to turn the criticism surrounding Sacramento into fuel for the upcoming season.

Under that interpretation, he was presenting the negative opinions outsiders had about the franchise and challenging the organization to prove them wrong.

That strategy carries an obvious risk for a team whose reputation has become synonymous with dysfunction. The Kings ended a 16-year playoff drought in 2023, but they have not returned to the postseason since.

Sacramento was 46-36 in 2023-24, fell to 40-42 the following season, and finished 2025-26 with a 22-60 record.

As long as Duke sticks to its core principles, the Blue Devils should finally earn their first win against Georgia Tech under Diaz. — Zach Ciavolella

articles.title: Steelers' Jalen Ramsey explodes over Joey Porter Jr. rumors
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers CB Jalen Ramsey went off on fans accusing him of influencing Joey Porter Jr.'s back injury controversy and eventual trade.
articles.body:
Jalen Ramsey has had enough! After many continued to speculate that the veteran defender played a role in Joey Porter Jr. 's "back injury" shenanigans and his eventual trade, Ramsey decided to set the record straight in a passionate post on social media.

On Friday, Ramsey called out fan rumors that he had anything to do with Porter's ugly situation with Pittsburgh. Although he supports Porter, Ramsey reminded fans that he's a Steeler first and foremost.

"Aye, yall are crazy lol…" Ramsey wrote via X. "The Joey narrative has to stop! I ain't tell no damn body to not play lol that's just flat out dumb! I still cheat when I play madden! I want to be teammates with good players! why would I tell a guy who I think is a top 5 corner to fake an injury (which I don't think he was doing anyways. The man was in the building tryna get right at 6 am [and] engaged in every meeting). Why would I not want a chance to suit up with him this year as a PITTSBURGH STEELER? Just doesn't make sense. Don't take me being in his corner the wrong way. His business is his business [and] I'm rocking wit him as my dawg… but I'm a Steeler [and] I want all good players to be apart of this team. I'm tryna win!"

It's understandable why some fans would believe Ramsey played a role in the way things played out for Porter in Pittsburgh. Ramsey's 2019 exit from the Jacksonville Jaguars was eerily similar to Porter's drama with the Steelers , which included a doubtful and mysterious "back injury" that ended up in a trade. Ramsey was also a huge mentor for Porter, and the two share the same agent in David Mulugheta. But Ramsey is adamant he had nothing to do with Porter's exit, despite the likely coincidental connections fans are making.
